timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Submits the NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1 for OSI certification, explaining that NASA-mandated indemnification, US federal law limits, usage tracking, anti-endorsement, and mandatory NOSA domination clauses make existing approved licenses insufficient.
timeline.point_zh: 提交 NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1 供 OSI 认证，说明 NASA 要求的免责赔偿、美国联邦法律限制、使用跟踪、禁止背书及 NOSA 强制主导条款使现有已批准许可证无法满足需要。
timeline.point: Submits the NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1 for OSI certification, explaining that NASA-mandated indemnification, US federal law limits, usage tracking, anti-endorsement, and mandatory NOSA domination clauses make existing approved licenses insufficient.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Questions the NASA license's indemnification and reporting requirements, noting disclaimers are standard and reporting unreasonably restricts licensees; argues reciprocity and other cited features already exist in OSL, GPL, MPL and CPL, so no new license is needed.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑 NASA 许可证的赔偿与报告要求，指出免责声明是标准做法而报告要求不合理地限制被许可人；互惠等特性在 OSL、GPL、MPL、CPL 中已有，无需另立新许可证。
timeline.point: Questions the NASA license's indemnification and reporting requirements, noting disclaimers are standard and reporting unreasonably restricts licensees; argues reciprocity and other cited features already exist in OSL, GPL, MPL and CPL, so no new license is needed.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Asks a series of questions about NOSA's registration requirement: whether downloading, reading documentation, or each version and installation triggers it, what happens when NASA's site is unreachable, and what 'statistical purposes' would cover.
timeline.point_zh: 就 NOSA 的注册要求提出一系列问题：下载、阅读文档或每个版本/安装是否都触发注册，NASA 网站不可用时如何处理，以及“统计目的”涵盖哪些情形。
timeline.point: Asks a series of questions about NOSA's registration requirement: whether downloading, reading documentation, or each version and installation triggers it, what happens when NASA's site is unreachable, and what 'statistical purposes' would cover.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Points out that NOSA only requires an "effort to track" rather than actual tracking, and that registration is only "requested" not "required".
timeline.point_zh: 指出 NOSA 只要求"努力追踪"而非实际追踪，且注册只是"请求"而非"要求"。
timeline.point: Points out that NOSA only requires an "effort to track" rather than actual tracking, and that registration is only "requested" not "required".

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Argues that if the intent is merely to show effort, the registration clause should be moved out of the license to avoid confusing non-native English speakers about its legal significance.
timeline.point_zh: 认为如果目的只是展示努力，注册条款应从许可证中移出，以免非英语母语者对其法律意义产生困惑。
timeline.point: Argues that if the intent is merely to show effort, the registration clause should be moved out of the license to avoid confusing non-native English speakers about its legal significance.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Argues the registration clause does not belong in the license itself, as it may deter users who don't want to register or consult a lawyer, and makes the license's open-source status ambiguous.
timeline.point_zh: 认为注册条款不应出现在许可证中，因为它可能阻止不愿注册或咨询律师的用户，并使许可证的开源地位变得模糊。
timeline.point: Argues the registration clause does not belong in the license itself, as it may deter users who don't want to register or consult a lawyer, and makes the license's open-source status ambiguous.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Defends the NASA license's liability, indemnification, and venue provisions against criticism, arguing its lawyer-drafted wording may be the best that money can buy and that 'armchair lawyer' nitpicking degrades the discussion.
timeline.point_zh: 为 NASA 许可证的责任、赔偿与管辖条款辩护，称其由专业律师起草、堪称最佳，并批评“扶手椅律师”式挑剔有损讨论价值。
timeline.point: Defends the NASA license's liability, indemnification, and venue provisions against criticism, arguing its lawyer-drafted wording may be the best that money can buy and that 'armchair lawyer' nitpicking degrades the discussion.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Corrects Richard Schilling that the mailing list exists to advise OSI on license approval, and clarifies that rejecting tracking requirements is about OSD compliance, not about the license being bad.
timeline.point_zh: 纠正 Richard Schilling 关于邮件列表的用途，明确拒绝追踪要求是关于 OSD 合规性，而非许可证本身的好坏。
timeline.point: Corrects Richard Schilling that the mailing list exists to advise OSI on license approval, and clarifies that rejecting tracking requirements is about OSD compliance, not about the license being bad.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Raises several concerns about the license: software written by civil servants would form a contract rather than a bare license, the missing mere-aggregation exception violates OSD section 9, and the sublicense termination clause discriminates based on whom one received the software from.
timeline.point_zh: 对该许可证提出多项关切：公务员编写的软件只能构成合同而非单纯许可，缺少聚合例外违反 OSD 第 9 条，再许可终止条款按软件来源歧视接收者。
timeline.point: Raises several concerns about the license: software written by civil servants would form a contract rather than a bare license, the missing mere-aggregation exception violates OSD section 9, and the sublicense termination clause discriminates based on whom one received the software from.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: States that the NASA license does not actually require tracking of released software.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 NASA 许可证实际上并不要求追踪已发布的软件。
timeline.point: States that the NASA license does not actually require tracking of released software.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Maintains that asking NASA to remove its indemnification wording is a heinous idea, that bashing the license on non-licensing issues harms open source development, and that tracking use per se does not make a license non-open-source.
timeline.point_zh: 坚持要求 NASA 删除赔偿条款是极糟的主意，以非许可问题抨击该许可证有损开源发展，且使用追踪本身并不会使许可证失去开源性质。
timeline.point: Maintains that asking NASA to remove its indemnification wording is a heinous idea, that bashing the license on non-licensing issues harms open source development, and that tracking use per se does not make a license non-open-source.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Rebuts the license's defense, arguing that OSD compliance matters regardless of the opportunity it offers: registration requirements could impede free distribution, and NASA should justify its one-sided indemnification clause that omits contributors.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳对该许可证的辩护，称无论机会多好都必须符合 OSD：注册要求可能妨碍自由分发，NASA 应说明其不含贡献者的单方赔偿条款的必要性。
timeline.point: Rebuts the license's defense, arguing that OSD compliance matters regardless of the opportunity it offers: registration requirements could impede free distribution, and NASA should justify its one-sided indemnification clause that omits contributors.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Defends the NASA license, arguing the waiver/indemnity clause is an administrative detail not barred by the OSD, criticizes the harsh tone toward NASA, and urges opensource.org to clarify its criteria, since copyright and waivers are not determinants of open source.
timeline.point_zh: 为 NASA 许可证辩护，称豁免赔偿条款只是 OSD 未禁止的行政细节，批评对 NASA 的苛刻语气，并主张版权与豁免不应作为开源的判定标准。
timeline.point: Defends the NASA license, arguing the waiver/indemnity clause is an administrative detail not barred by the OSD, criticizes the harsh tone toward NASA, and urges opensource.org to clarify its criteria, since copyright and waivers are not determinants of open source.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that Larry only offered initial thoughts and no rejection has been made; notes he has identified situations he believes violate the OSD (uncertain on the indemnification itself), and expects the license will eventually be approved with minor modifications.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清 Larry 只是初步意见，尚无人要求否决；称自己发现该许可证有几处疑似违反 OSD（赔偿条款本身不确定），预计小幅修改后最终会获批。
timeline.point: Clarifies that Larry only offered initial thoughts and no rejection has been made; notes he has identified situations he believes violate the OSD (uncertain on the indemnification itself), and expects the license will eventually be approved with minor modifications.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Points out that IPL/CPL section 4 contains an indemnification clause, countering the claim that no OSI-certified license includes one.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 IPL/CPL 第 4 条包含免责条款，反驳了没有 OSI 认证许可证包含免责条款的说法。
timeline.point: Points out that IPL/CPL section 4 contains an indemnification clause, countering the claim that no OSI-certified license includes one.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Argues works by U.S. Government employees cannot be copyrighted under Title 17, so NASA software needs no license and any license would be trumped by copyright law; asks how NASA's policy, Title 17, and the proposed license can be reconciled.
timeline.point_zh: 认为美国政府雇员作品依 Title 17 不受版权保护，NASA 软件无需许可证且任何许可证都会被版权法推翻；询问 NASA 政策、Title 17 与该许可证如何调和。
timeline.point: Argues works by U.S. Government employees cannot be copyrighted under Title 17, so NASA software needs no license and any license would be trumped by copyright law; asks how NASA's policy, Title 17, and the proposed license can be reconciled.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Notes that NOSA correctly disclaims copyright for civil servant works within the U.S. but claims copyright outside the U.S., which is a novel and potentially significant legal point.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 NOSA 在美国境内正确地放弃了公务员作品的版权，但在美国境外主张版权，这是一个新颖且潜在重要的法律观点。
timeline.point: Notes that NOSA correctly disclaims copyright for civil servant works within the U.S. but claims copyright outside the U.S., which is a novel and potentially significant legal point.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Explains why tracking requirements are inappropriate in open source licenses: it could make distribution impossible if the tracking organization disappears, prevents anonymous use which violates OSD #5, and contradicts FSF principles.
timeline.point_zh: 解释为什么追踪要求不适合出现在开源许可证中：追踪组织消失可能导致分发不可能、阻止匿名使用违反 OSD #5、且与 FSF 原则相悖。
timeline.point: Explains why tracking requirements are inappropriate in open source licenses: it could make distribution impossible if the tracking organization disappears, prevents anonymous use which violates OSD #5, and contradicts FSF principles.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Rejects the idea that only distribution matters for open-source status, stating the OSD imposes additional requirements, and suggests proposing specific OSD changes if modifications are desired.
timeline.point_zh: 拒绝仅以分发作为开源标准的观点，指出 OSD 有额外要求，并建议如需修改应提出具体的 OSD 变更建议。
timeline.point: Rejects the idea that only distribution matters for open-source status, stating the OSD imposes additional requirements, and suggests proposing specific OSD changes if modifications are desired.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Reiterates confusion about NOSA's legal basis, arguing that Title 17 makes government works public domain everywhere, leaving no copyright to license.
timeline.point_zh: 重申对 NOSA 法律基础的困惑，认为 Title 17 使政府作品在所有地方都进入公共领域，没有可供许可的版权。
timeline.point: Reiterates confusion about NOSA's legal basis, arguing that Title 17 makes government works public domain everywhere, leaving no copyright to license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Explains that through the Berne Convention, works can be in the public domain in the U.S. but copyrighted elsewhere, and raises the unresolved conflict-of-laws question of whether a work born into the public domain can be copyrighted in another country.
timeline.point_zh: 解释通过《伯尔尼公约》，作品可以在美国进入公共领域但在他国受版权保护，并提出作品在其原产国进入公共领域后能否在他国获得版权的冲突法问题。
timeline.point: Explains that through the Berne Convention, works can be in the public domain in the U.S. but copyrighted elsewhere, and raises the unresolved conflict-of-laws question of whether a work born into the public domain can be copyrighted in another country.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges that indemnification clauses exist in other OSI-approved licenses, and while uncomfortable with the broad waiver in NOSA, does not believe it rises to the level of OSD rejection.
timeline.point_zh: 承认免责条款在其他 OSI 批准的许可证中存在，虽然对 NOSA 中的宽泛免责感到不适，但认为不足以构成 OSD 拒绝的理由。
timeline.point: Acknowledges that indemnification clauses exist in other OSI-approved licenses, and while uncomfortable with the broad waiver in NOSA, does not believe it rises to the level of OSD rejection.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Defends the NASA license's tracking provision, arguing web-log tracking is routine, that non-discrimination only requires unrestricted access, and that NASA's enforced registration is more consistent than the GNU license's unenforced change-submission requirement.
timeline.point_zh: 为 NASA 许可证的跟踪条款辩护，称网络日志跟踪属常规、非歧视只要求不限制获取，且 NASA 严格执行注册比 GNU 许可证形同虚设的修改回馈要求更一致。
timeline.point: Defends the NASA license's tracking provision, arguing web-log tracking is routine, that non-discrimination only requires unrestricted access, and that NASA's enforced registration is more consistent than the GNU license's unenforced change-submission requirement.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Confirms that under the Berne Convention, a work can be in the public domain in its country of origin but copyrighted elsewhere, citing relevant articles.
timeline.point_zh: 确认根据《伯尔尼公约》，作品可以在其原产国进入公共领域但在他国受版权保护，引用了相关条款。
timeline.point: Confirms that under the Berne Convention, a work can be in the public domain in its country of origin but copyrighted elsewhere, citing relevant articles.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Distinguishes benign tracking of direct downloaders from the NASA license's request that every recipient register; argues that a mandatory registration would violate the OSD, and that a vanished registration site could later block legal distribution.
timeline.point_zh: 区分对直接下载者的良性跟踪与 NASA 许可证请求每位接收者注册的做法；指出若注册成为强制要求将违反 OSD，且注册网站消失可能日后阻碍合法分发。
timeline.point: Distinguishes benign tracking of direct downloaders from the NASA license's request that every recipient register; argues that a mandatory registration would violate the OSD, and that a vanished registration site could later block legal distribution.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Concludes that U.S. government works are in the public domain domestically but copyrighted for 50 years in Australia, meaning Americans can ignore NOSA for civil-servant works but Australians cannot.
timeline.point_zh: 得出结论：美国政府作品在美国境内属公共领域但在澳大利亚受 50 年版权保护，因此美国人可以无视 NOSA 中公务员版本但澳大利亚人不行。
timeline.point: Concludes that U.S. government works are in the public domain domestically but copyrighted for 50 years in Australia, meaning Americans can ignore NOSA for civil-servant works but Australians cannot.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Summarizes three options for NASA's registration clause: (1) move voluntary requests out of the license, (2) stop tricking users if not legally required, or (3) make registration a clear legal requirement, which would likely prevent OSI certification.
timeline.point_zh: 总结 NASA 注册条款的三种选择：（1）将自愿请求移出许可证，（2）如非法律要求则停止误导用户，（3）使注册成为明确的法律要求（但这可能导致无法通过 OSI 认证）。
timeline.point: Summarizes three options for NASA's registration clause: (1) move voluntary requests out of the license, (2) stop tricking users if not legally required, or (3) make registration a clear legal requirement, which would likely prevent OSI certification.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Asks NASA to remove both the tracking clause and the indemnification clause from the license for simplicity, suggesting the tracking request belongs in documentation instead.
timeline.point_zh: 建议 NASA 出于简化目的从许可证中删除追踪条款和免责条款，认为追踪请求应放在文档中。
timeline.point: Asks NASA to remove both the tracking clause and the indemnification clause from the license for simplicity, suggesting the tracking request belongs in documentation instead.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Strongly argues that tracking software usage is fundamentally incompatible with Free/Libre and Open Source Software principles, and warns against OSI weakening the Open Source Definition to accommodate tracking requirements.
timeline.point_zh: 强烈主张追踪软件使用与自由/开源软件原则根本不兼容，并警告 OSI 不应为迁就追踪要求而削弱开源定义。
timeline.point: Strongly argues that tracking software usage is fundamentally incompatible with Free/Libre and Open Source Software principles, and warns against OSI weakening the Open Source Definition to accommodate tracking requirements.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Argues that requiring redistributors to ask users to register is not unreasonable and does not violate the OSD, comparing it to the GPL's requirement to display certain text at startup.
timeline.point_zh: 认为要求分发者请求用户注册并非不合理且不违反 OSD，并将其与 GPL 要求程序启动时显示特定文本进行类比。
timeline.point: Argues that requiring redistributors to ask users to register is not unreasonable and does not violate the OSD, comparing it to the GPL's requirement to display certain text at startup.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Agrees with Russ Nelson that requiring redistributors to ask for registration is acceptable, but notes this falls under the case where NASA should make the legal requirement explicit in the license.
timeline.point_zh: 同意 Russ Nelson 关于要求分发者请求注册是可接受的观点，但指出这属于 NASA 应在许可证中明确法律要求的情况。
timeline.point: Agrees with Russ Nelson that requiring redistributors to ask for registration is acceptable, but notes this falls under the case where NASA should make the legal requirement explicit in the license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Asks what happens when a US citizen redistributes public domain US Government software in Australia, noting the NOSA will likely fix this jurisdictional issue.
timeline.point_zh: 询问当美国公民在美国公有领域政府软件在澳大利亚重新分发时会发生什么，认为 NOSA 将解决这一管辖权问题。
timeline.point: Asks what happens when a US citizen redistributes public domain US Government software in Australia, noting the NOSA will likely fix this jurisdictional issue.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Points out that NOSA covers patent rights in addition to copyrights, and that the US Government may not have restrictions on patent ownership.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 NOSA 不仅涵盖版权还涵盖专利权，且美国政府在专利所有权方面可能不受限制。
timeline.point: Points out that NOSA covers patent rights in addition to copyrights, and that the US Government may not have restrictions on patent ownership.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Asks whether someone who downloads public domain US Government code via FOIA can relicense it under a BSD license, questioning the right to relicense public domain works.
timeline.point_zh: 询问通过 FOIA 下载公有领域美国政府代码后是否可以将其重新授权为 BSD 许可证，质疑重新授权公有领域作品的权利。
timeline.point: Asks whether someone who downloads public domain US Government code via FOIA can relicense it under a BSD license, questioning the right to relicense public domain works.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Explains that you can do anything with a public domain work except assert valid copyright on it, which is required by BSD and other open-source licenses, so relicensing under BSD is not possible.
timeline.point_zh: 解释对公有领域作品可以做任何事，但不能对其主张有效版权，而 BSD 等开源许可证需要这一权利，因此无法重新授权。
timeline.point: Explains that you can do anything with a public domain work except assert valid copyright on it, which is required by BSD and other open-source licenses, so relicensing under BSD is not possible.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Expresses confusion about whether one can create derivative works of public domain code and release them under a chosen license, such as incorporating PD code into Apache httpd.
timeline.point_zh: 对是否可以创建公有领域代码的衍生作品并以自己选择的许可证发布表示困惑，例如将 PD 代码整合到 Apache httpd 中。
timeline.point: Expresses confusion about whether one can create derivative works of public domain code and release them under a chosen license, such as incorporating PD code into Apache httpd.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that creating derivative works of public domain code is allowed, but claiming copyright on the original public domain work itself is not. Raises the follow-up question about extracting public domain parts from a BSD-licensed derivative.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清可以创建公有领域代码的衍生作品，但不能对原始公有领域作品主张版权。提出后续问题：是否可以从 BSD 许可的衍生作品中提取公有领域部分。
timeline.point: Clarifies that creating derivative works of public domain code is allowed, but claiming copyright on the original public domain work itself is not. Raises the follow-up question about extracting public domain parts from a BSD-licensed derivative.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Confirms that creating derivative works of public domain code is allowed, but the derivative work must be genuinely derivative and not just a minor modification.
timeline.point_zh: 确认可以创建公有领域代码的衍生作品，但衍生作品必须是真正的衍生作品，而不仅仅是对原始公有领域代码的轻微修改。
timeline.point: Confirms that creating derivative works of public domain code is allowed, but the derivative work must be genuinely derivative and not just a minor modification.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Agrees that Brian is correct: you can add value to public domain works and license the enhanced version, create derivative works, or simply distribute it better, but the original work remains in the public domain.
timeline.point_zh: 同意 Brian 的观点：可以为公有领域作品增值并许可增强版本、创建衍生作品，或更好地分发原始作品，但原始作品仍处于公有领域。
timeline.point: Agrees that Brian is correct: you can add value to public domain works and license the enhanced version, create derivative works, or simply distribute it better, but the original work remains in the public domain.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Resolves the confusion by confirming both parties are right: nobody can assert copyright on a public domain work itself, but anyone can create a derivative work and license it under any license.
timeline.point_zh: 通过确认双方都正确来解决分歧：没有人可以对公有领域作品本身主张版权，但任何人都可以创建衍生作品并以任何许可证分发。
timeline.point: Resolves the confusion by confirming both parties are right: nobody can assert copyright on a public domain work itself, but anyone can create a derivative work and license it under any license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Disagrees with John's characterization, arguing that anyone can do anything to a public domain work without a license, and the real question is whether the derivative work has sufficient creativity to be copyrightable.
timeline.point_zh: 不同意 John 的表述，认为任何人都可以对公有领域作品做任何事而无需许可，真正的问题是衍生作品是否具有足够的创造性以获得版权保护。
timeline.point: Disagrees with John's characterization, arguing that anyone can do anything to a public domain work without a license, and the real question is whether the derivative work has sufficient creativity to be copyrightable.

timeline.subject: For Approval: NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.1
timeline.snippet: Agrees that the degree of creativity matters, and clarifies that while one cannot fraudulently claim copyright on unmodified public domain code, one can create a genuinely derivative work and apply one's own copyright and license to it.
timeline.point_zh: 同意创造性程度是关键问题，澄清虽然不能欺诈性地对未修改的公有领域代码主张版权，但可以创建真正的衍生作品并应用自己的版权和许可证。
timeline.point: Agrees that the degree of creativity matters, and clarifies that while one cannot fraudulently claim copyright on unmodified public domain code, one can create a genuinely derivative work and apply one's own copyright and license to it.

KEY:

Below is an OSSAL template.  To generate your own license, change the values of <AUTHOR>, <RELEASE>, <SOFTWARE>, and <YEARS> from their original values as given here, and substitute your own.

  <RELEASE> = FreeBSD 5.3 (ex: "FreeBSD 5.3", "PostgreSQL 7.4")

   with any software license that requires disclosure of source
   code (ex: the GNU Public License, hereafter known as the GPL).
5. Redistributions of source code in any non-textual form (i.e.
   binary or object form, etc.) may not be linked to software that is
   released with a license that requires disclosure of source code
   (ex: the GPL).

ANY EXPRESS OR IMPLIED WARRANTIES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, THE
IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR
PURPOSE ARE DISCLAIMED.  IN NO EVENT SHALL <AUTHOR> OR CONTRIBUTORS BE
LIABLE FOR ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR
CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES (INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PROCUREMENT OF
SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES; LOSS OF USE, DATA, OR PROFITS; OR
BUSINESS INTERRUPTION) HOWEVER CAUSED AND ON ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY,
WHETHER IN CONTRACT, STRICT LIABILITY, OR TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE
OR OTHERWISE) ARISING IN ANY WAY OUT OF THE USE OF THIS SOFTWARE, EVEN
IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE.
### END TEMPLATE ###


DISCUSSION:


    The Open Source Software Alliance (hereafter known as "OSSAL"), is
designed to be a business friendly Open Source Software license that
encourages businesses to release or make use of OSSAL software (OSSAL
is a BSDL-like license).  The intent of OSSAL is akin to the phrase,
"if you scratch my back, I'll scratch your back."  With OSSAL
software, a business is able to use and incorporate existing software
that is licensed under the OSSAL or other BSDL-like licenses.  The
incorporated software can be sold.  A business can lend resources to
an OSSAL project and not waive its right to make money from the
software.  By allowing other businesses to have access to non-trade
secret software under the terms of the OSSAL, other businesses can
invest in improving the software.  Both businesses win by
collaborating.  If a business keeps the changes in house and does not
contribute them back to the project, the business incurs a reoccurring
cost for maintaining that software.  The joint nature of OSSAL
software reduces maintenance costs of software.  The extra engineers
and eyes inspecting the code will increase the quality of the code in
terms of functionality and reduce the number of bugs.  OSSAL is
software reciprocity.

    If a business invests in software released under the terms of the GPL
(or a GPL-like license), the money that the business invested into
developing the software is unrecoverable because the software that was
the target of the investment is not commercially viable to the
business that invested in the development effort[1].  The exception to
the software's viability is being able to provide support or
documentation for the software.  If a business manager or engineer
realizes this, one of two things will happen: 1) he or she is going to
dedicate as little resources as possible into solving the problem
because work on GPL software has zero return on investment outside of
satisfying a business's immediate needs, or 2) he or she is going to
realize that it is of no consequence to the business if the quality of
the investment is high or low, therefore they are going to err on the
side of providing a lower quality, less well thought out solution
because it could drive documentation sales or support contracts.

    As for software quality, if the theories of capitalism are true, and
the job market is a functioning market place (the higher the skilled
engineer, the more the engineer is paid.  The more the engineer is
paid, the busier the engineer is.  The more complex product generates
more income and consumes more engineering resources of increasing
skill, thus depriving the open source community of the talents of a
skilled engineer), then businesses with the most qualified engineers
are not working on any percentage of Open Source software.  By
allowing engineers to work on software that is usable by their
business, the quality of the tools of the product that the business
produces, will go up.  By Open Sourcing non-trade secret software
under the OSSAL license, it is now possible, and very potentially
likely that other businesses will invest resources into improving the
OSSAL software.  The corollary to the above statement is that the most
expendable, unimportant engineers work on GPL software and the better
software engineers work on BSDL-licensed software.

    The goal of this license is to promote businesses to open source
non-trade secret software and to contribute resources, when necessary,
to OSSAL or BSDL licensed software.  With multiple businesses using
and working on necessary bug fixes, updates, etc.: the cost of
software development, maintenance, and support goes down; the number
of bugs goes down, and; the quality of the software and its
documentation goes up.  OSSAL also discourages the use of GPL or viral
licenses as they indirectly promote lower quality software that is
widely disseminated, but not reviewed by the more highly skilled
software engineers.  By getting a group of businesses to use and
dedicate resources to OSSAL software, the group of businesses have
created an off the books, informal alliance to help one another.  "If
you scratch my back, I'll scratch yours."
  


FOOTNOTES:


  [1] The GPL requires free availability of the source code for a
product (can only charge for shipping and the material cost of the CD,
disks, etc.), requires that the recipient of the code be bound by the
GPL as well, and requires that any product that uses GPL code, also be
bound to the terms of the GPL (requiring it to be open source and
distributed free of charge if the product is sold).


DOWNLOADS:
An HTML copy of the license can be found at: http://people.FreeBSD.org/~seanc/ossal/ossal.html


COMMENTS, QUESTIONS, and DISCUSSION
If you have any comments, questions, concerns, or would like to discuss this license, please direct them to "Sean Chittenden <sean at chittenden.org>.

DISCUSSION:


    The Open Source Software Alliance (hereafter known as "OSSAL"), is
designed to be a business friendly Open Source Software license that
encourages businesses to release or make use of OSSAL software (OSSAL
is a BSDL-like license).  The intent of OSSAL is akin to the phrase,
"if you scratch my back, I'll scratch your back."  With OSSAL
software, a business is able to use and incorporate existing software
that is licensed under the OSSAL or other BSDL-like licenses.  The
incorporated software can be sold.  A business can lend resources to
an OSSAL project and not waive its right to make money from the
software.  By allowing other businesses to have access to non-trade
secret software under the terms of the OSSAL, other businesses can
invest in improving the software.  Both businesses win by
collaborating.  If a business keeps the changes in house and does not
contribute them back to the project, the business incurs a reoccurring
cost for maintaining that software.  The joint nature of OSSAL
software reduces maintenance costs of software.  The extra engineers
and eyes inspecting the code will increase the quality of the code in
terms of functionality and reduce the number of bugs.  OSSAL is
software reciprocity.

    If a business invests in software released under the terms of the GPL
(or a GPL-like license), the money that the business invested into
developing the software is unrecoverable because the software that was
the target of the investment is not commercially viable to the
business that invested in the development effort[1].  The exception to
the software's viability is being able to provide support or
documentation for the software.  If a business manager or engineer
realizes this, one of two things will happen: 1) he or she is going to
dedicate as little resources as possible into solving the problem
because work on GPL software has zero return on investment outside of
satisfying a business's immediate needs, or 2) he or she is going to
realize that it is of no consequence to the business if the quality of
the investment is high or low, therefore they are going to err on the
side of providing a lower quality, less well thought out solution
because it could drive documentation sales or support contracts.

    As for software quality, if the theories of capitalism are true, and
the job market is a functioning market place (the higher the skilled
engineer, the more the engineer is paid.  The more the engineer is
paid, the busier the engineer is.  The more complex product generates
more income and consumes more engineering resources of increasing
skill, thus depriving the open source community of the talents of a
skilled engineer), then businesses with the most qualified engineers
are not working on any percentage of Open Source software.  By
allowing engineers to work on software that is usable by their
business, the quality of the tools of the product that the business
produces, will go up.  By Open Sourcing non-trade secret software
under the OSSAL license, it is now possible, and very potentially
likely that other businesses will invest resources into improving the
OSSAL software.  The corollary to the above statement is that the most
expendable, unimportant engineers work on GPL software and the better
software engineers work on BSDL-licensed software.

    The goal of this license is to promote businesses to open source
non-trade secret software and to contribute resources, when necessary,
to OSSAL or BSDL licensed software.  With multiple businesses using
and working on necessary bug fixes, updates, etc.: the cost of
software development, maintenance, and support goes down; the number
of bugs goes down, and; the quality of the software and its
documentation goes up.  OSSAL also discourages the use of GPL or viral
licenses as they indirectly promote lower quality software that is
widely disseminated, but not reviewed by the more highly skilled
software engineers.  By getting a group of businesses to use and
dedicate resources to OSSAL software, the group of businesses have
created an off the books, informal alliance to help one another.  "If
you scratch my back, I'll scratch yours."



FOOTNOTES:


  [1] The GPL requires free availability of the source code for a
product (can only charge for shipping and the material cost of the CD,
disks, etc.), requires that the recipient of the code be bound by the
GPL as well, and requires that any product that uses GPL code, also be
bound to the terms of the GPL (requiring it to be open source and
distributed free of charge if the product is sold).


DOWNLOADS:
An HTML copy of the license can be found at: http://people.FreeBSD.org/~seanc/ossal/ossal.html


COMMENTS, QUESTIONS, and DISCUSSION
If you have any comments, questions, concerns, or would like to discuss this license, please direct them to "Sean Chittenden <sean at chittenden.org>.

DISCUSSION:
The Open Source Software Alliance (hereafter known as "OSSAL"), is
designed to be a business friendly Open Source Software license that
encourages businesses to release or make use of OSSAL software (OSSAL
is a BSDL-like license).  The intent of OSSAL is akin to the phrase,
"if you scratch my back, I'll scratch your back."  With OSSAL
software, a business is able to use and incorporate existing software
that is licensed under the OSSAL or other BSDL-like licenses.  The
incorporated software can be sold.  A business can lend resources to
an OSSAL project and not waive its right to make money from the
software.  By allowing other businesses to have access to non-trade
secret software under the terms of the OSSAL, other businesses can
invest in improving the software.  Both businesses win by
collaborating.  If a business keeps the changes in house and does not
contribute them back to the project, the business incurs a reoccurring
cost for maintaining that software.  The joint nature of OSSAL
software reduces maintenance costs of software.  The extra engineers
and eyes inspecting the code will increase the quality of the code in
terms of functionality and reduce the number of bugs.  OSSAL is
software reciprocity.
If a business invests in software released under the terms of the GPL
(or a GPL-like license), the money that the business invested into
developing the software is unrecoverable because the software that was
the target of the investment is not commercially viable to the
business that invested in the development effort[1].  The exception to
the software's viability is being able to provide support or
documentation for the software.  If a business manager or engineer
realizes this, one of two things will happen: 1) he or she is going to
dedicate as little resources as possible into solving the problem
because work on GPL software has zero return on investment outside of
satisfying a business's immediate needs, or 2) he or she is going to
realize that it is of no consequence to the business if the quality of
the investment is high or low, therefore they are going to err on the
side of providing a lower quality, less well thought out solution
because it could drive documentation sales or support contracts.
As for software quality, if the theories of capitalism are true, and
the job market is a functioning market place (the higher the skilled
engineer, the more the engineer is paid.  The more the engineer is
paid, the busier the engineer is.  The more complex product generates
more income and consumes more engineering resources of increasing
skill, thus depriving the open source community of the talents of a
skilled engineer), then businesses with the most qualified engineers
are not working on any percentage of Open Source software.  By
allowing engineers to work on software that is usable by their
business, the quality of the tools of the product that the business
produces, will go up.  By Open Sourcing non-trade secret software
under the OSSAL license, it is now possible, and very potentially
likely that other businesses will invest resources into improving the
OSSAL software.  The corollary to the above statement is that the most
expendable, unimportant engineers work on GPL software and the better
software engineers work on BSDL-licensed software.
The goal of this license is to promote businesses to open source
non-trade secret software and to contribute resources, when necessary,
to OSSAL or BSDL licensed software.  With multiple businesses using
and working on necessary bug fixes, updates, etc.: the cost of
software development, maintenance, and support goes down; the number
of bugs goes down, and; the quality of the software and its
documentation goes up.  OSSAL also discourages the use of GPL or viral
licenses as they indirectly promote lower quality software that is
widely disseminated, but not reviewed by the more highly skilled
software engineers.  By getting a group of businesses to use and
dedicate resources to OSSAL software, the group of businesses have
created an off the books, informal alliance to help one another.  "If
you scratch my back, I'll scratch yours."
FOOTNOTES:
[1] The GPL requires free availability of the source code for a
product (can only charge for shipping and the material cost of the CD,
disks, etc.), requires that the recipient of the code be bound by the
GPL as well, and requires that any product that uses GPL code, also be
bound to the terms of the GPL (requiring it to be open source and
distributed free of charge if the product is sold).

true, and the job market is a functioning market place (the higher the
skilled engineer, the more the engineer is paid.  The more the
engineer is paid, the busier the engineer is.  The more complex
product generates more income and consumes more engineering resources
of increasing skill, thus depriving the open source community of the
talents of a skilled engineer), then businesses with the most
qualified engineers are not working on any percentage of Open Source
software.  By allowing engineers to work on software that is usable by
their business, the quality of the tools of the product that the
business produces, will go up.  By Open Sourcing non-trade secret
software under the OSSAL license, it is now possible, and very
potentially likely that other businesses will invest resources into
improving the OSSAL software.  The corollary to the above statement is
that the most expendable, unimportant engineers work on GPL software
and the better software engineers work on BSDL-licensed software.
The goal of this license is to promote businesses to open
source non-trade secret software and to contribute resources, when
necessary, to OSSAL or BSDL licensed software.  With multiple
businesses using and working on necessary bug fixes, updates, etc.:
the cost of software development, maintenance, and support goes down;
the number of bugs goes down, and; the quality of the software and its
documentation goes up.  OSSAL also discourages the use of GPL or viral
licenses as they indirectly promote lower quality software that is
widely disseminated, but not reviewed by the more highly skilled
software engineers.  By getting a group of businesses to use and
dedicate resources to OSSAL software, the group of businesses have
created an off the books, informal alliance to help one another.  "If
you scratch my back, I'll scratch yours."

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Submitting the OSSAL, a derivative of the BSD license that prevents code from being used with GPL'ed code, for OSI approval, with a clause-by-clause analysis.
timeline.point_zh: 提交 OSSAL——一个防止代码与 GPL 代码一同使用的 BSD 衍生许可证——供 OSI 审批，并附逐条分析。
timeline.point: Submitting the OSSAL, a derivative of the BSD license that prevents code from being used with GPL'ed code, for OSI approval, with a clause-by-clause analysis.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Encourages dropping the license since BSD-style code should allow linking with GPL code; questions the advertising clause's clarity, and says he would vote against approval as it may balkanize the open source community despite arguably meeting the OSD.
timeline.point_zh: 劝阻使用该许可证，因 BSD 式代码应可与 GPL 代码链接；质疑广告条款的清晰性，并称即便可能符合 OSD，为免分裂开源社区他仍会投反对票。
timeline.point: Encourages dropping the license since BSD-style code should allow linking with GPL code; questions the advertising clause's clarity, and says he would vote against approval as it may balkanize the open source community despite arguably meeting the OSD.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues BSD or MIT would serve the stated purpose better than OSSAL, which imposes an unnecessary burden by preventing businesses from using GPL code.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 BSD 或 MIT 许可证比 OSSAL 更适合其目的，因为 OSSAL 给企业施加了无法使用 GPL 代码的不必要负担。
timeline.point: Argues BSD or MIT would serve the stated purpose better than OSSAL, which imposes an unnecessary burden by preventing businesses from using GPL code.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Agrees the license conforms to the OSD, clarifies that the advertising clause is non-binding due to 'should', explains the GPL restriction targets derivative works not relicensing, and recommends changing 'may not' to 'must not' for clarity.
timeline.point_zh: 同意许可证符合 OSD，澄清广告条款因使用'should'而无约束力，解释 GPL 限制针对衍生作品而非重新授权，并建议将'may not'改为'must not'以避免误解。
timeline.point: Agrees the license conforms to the OSD, clarifies that the advertising clause is non-binding due to 'should', explains the GPL restriction targets derivative works not relicensing, and recommends changing 'may not' to 'must not' for clarity.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Defends the OSSAL's intent of keeping modules business-friendly and non-GPL, clarifies the advertising clause is not mandatory, and adds a new clause 6 barring removal of OSSAL terms to prevent relicensing.
timeline.point_zh: 为 OSSAL 辩护：保持模块对商业友好、不受 GPL 影响，澄清广告条款并非强制，并新增第 6 条禁止移除 OSSAL 条款以防改用其他许可。
timeline.point: Defends the OSSAL's intent of keeping modules business-friendly and non-GPL, clarifies the advertising clause is not mandatory, and adds a new clause 6 barring removal of OSSAL terms to prevent relicensing.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges the suggestion to change 'may not' to 'must not' and confirms the license wording has been updated accordingly.
timeline.point_zh: 认可将'may not'改为'must not'的建议，并确认许可证措辞已相应更新。
timeline.point: Acknowledges the suggestion to change 'may not' to 'must not' and confirms the license wording has been updated accordingly.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues GPL-using businesses like Cygnus thrive, that the OSSAL forces duplicated work just as the GPL does and is less free than FreeBSD, and that confusion should be addressed by education rather than a community-weakening license.
timeline.point_zh: 指出使用 GPL 的 Cygnus 等企业同样成功，认为 OSSAL 与 GPL 一样导致重复劳动、不如 FreeBSD 自由，应以教育化解误解而非推行削弱社区的许可证。
timeline.point: Argues GPL-using businesses like Cygnus thrive, that the OSSAL forces duplicated work just as the GPL does and is less free than FreeBSD, and that confusion should be addressed by education rather than a community-weakening license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that clause 5 targets OSSAL source code only, so linking with LGPL libraries remains allowed; explains the license's business focus and term 6's anti-relicensing purpose, and asks to keep GPL-advocacy debate off the list.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清第 5 条仅针对 OSSAL 源代码，故仍可与 LGPL 库链接；说明该许可证面向商业的定位及第 6 条防改许可的用意，并请求勿在本列表讨论倡导 GPL 的题外话题。
timeline.point: Clarifies that clause 5 targets OSSAL source code only, so linking with LGPL libraries remains allowed; explains the license's business focus and term 6's anti-relicensing purpose, and asks to keep GPL-advocacy debate off the list.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues GPLv2 cannot 'require' disclosure of an OSSAL-covered work's source—mere linkage triggers no source-access obligation and the GPL has no authority over others' code—so the OSSAL provision attempts to cure a nonexistent problem.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 GPLv2 无法'要求'公开 OSSAL 覆盖代码的源码:仅链接不触发源码公开义务,GPL 对他人代码也无管辖权,该条款在解决一个不存在的问题。
timeline.point: Argues GPLv2 cannot 'require' disclosure of an OSSAL-covered work's source—mere linkage triggers no source-access obligation and the GPL has no authority over others' code—so the OSSAL provision attempts to cure a nonexistent problem.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Supports Sean's position by noting that Bruce Perens, a prominent GPL advocate, also stated that the GPL has limited commercial applications.
timeline.point_zh: 支持 Sean 的立场，指出 GPL 的积极倡导者 Bruce Perens 也曾表示 GPL 的商业应用有限。
timeline.point: Supports Sean's position by noting that Bruce Perens, a prominent GPL advocate, also stated that the GPL has limited commercial applications.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Counters that the GPL does not interfere with commerce but with creating proprietary software, and that conflating 'business' with 'commerce' obscures this essential distinction.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳称 GPL 不干涉商业活动而是干涉创建专有软件，将'商业'与'商业活动'混为一谈模糊了这一关键区别。
timeline.point: Counters that the GPL does not interfere with commerce but with creating proprietary software, and that conflating 'business' with 'commerce' obscures this essential distinction.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues that inheritive licenses like the GPL are premier commercial licenses under a dual-licensing scheme when the distributor owns all copyrights, and warns against locking into a single business model.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 GPL 等继承性许可证在掌握全部版权时可通过双许可成为一流商业许可,并告诫不要像 RIAA 那样固守单一商业模式。
timeline.point: Argues that inheritive licenses like the GPL are premier commercial licenses under a dual-licensing scheme when the distributor owns all copyrights, and warns against locking into a single business model.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges the GPL interferes with proprietary software creation and explains this is exactly why the OSSAL was created, to give businesses the ability to create proprietary software from open source components.
timeline.point_zh: 承认 GPL 干涉专有软件的创建，解释这正是创建 OSSAL 的原因，旨在让企业能够从开源组件创建专有软件。
timeline.point: Acknowledges the GPL interferes with proprietary software creation and explains this is exactly why the OSSAL was created, to give businesses the ability to create proprietary software from open source components.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Agrees to add an FAQ for clause clarity, argues the GPL is problematic because it prevents shipping products, and defends clause 6 as an explicit reminder against historical license dilution cases.
timeline.point_zh: 同意为条款清晰度添加 FAQ，主张 GPL 有问题因为它阻止产品发布，并为条款 6 辩护，认为它是对历史许可稀释案例的明确提醒。
timeline.point: Agrees to add an FAQ for clause clarity, argues the GPL is problematic because it prevents shipping products, and defends clause 6 as an explicit reminder against historical license dilution cases.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues the OSSAL provides no business guarantee beyond the BSD license, that clause 6 is unnecessary since original OSSAL code retains its license, and that OSI as a political organization makes this debate on-topic.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 OSSAL 未提供超出 BSD 许可证的商业保障，条款 6 是不必要的因为原始 OSSAL 代码保留其许可证，并认为 OSI 作为政治组织使此辩论是切题的。
timeline.point: Argues the OSSAL provides no business guarantee beyond the BSD license, that clause 6 is unnecessary since original OSSAL code retains its license, and that OSI as a political organization makes this debate on-topic.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Points out that the BSD license already allows businesses to create proprietary software, making the OSSAL's stated purpose redundant.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 BSD 许可证已允许企业创建专有软件，使 OSSAL 的既定目的显得多余。
timeline.point: Points out that the BSD license already allows businesses to create proprietary software, making the OSSAL's stated purpose redundant.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Counters that while BSD permits proprietary forks, it does not ensure all derivative software remains under business-friendly terms, which is the core purpose of the OSSAL.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳称虽然 BSD 允许专有分支，但不能确保所有衍生软件都保持商业友好条款，这正是 OSSAL 的核心目的。
timeline.point: Counters that while BSD permits proprietary forks, it does not ensure all derivative software remains under business-friendly terms, which is the core purpose of the OSSAL.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Analyzes the OSSAL as a 'reverse copyleft' that permits proprietary forks but prohibits GPL forks, whose only real effect is prohibiting the prohibition of proprietary forks; concludes it doesn't seem useful.
timeline.point_zh: 将 OSSAL 分析为'反向 copyleft':允许专有分叉却禁止 GPL 分叉,唯一实际效果是禁止'禁止专有分叉',认为该许可证没什么用。
timeline.point: Analyzes the OSSAL as a 'reverse copyleft' that permits proprietary forks but prohibits GPL forks, whose only real effect is prohibiting the prohibition of proprietary forks; concludes it doesn't seem useful.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Confirms the OSSAL is designed to prohibit GPL forks while explicitly permitting proprietary forks, and argues businesses benefit because they never have to rewrite dependent code if a module author goes copyleft, encouraging more business use of open source.
timeline.point_zh: 确认 OSSAL 旨在禁止 GPL 分叉、明确允许专有分叉,并认为这让企业无需担心依赖代码被转成 copyleft 而重写,有助于企业使用并回馈开源。
timeline.point: Confirms the OSSAL is designed to prohibit GPL forks while explicitly permitting proprietary forks, and argues businesses benefit because they never have to rewrite dependent code if a module author goes copyleft, encouraging more business use of open source.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Questions the commercial/noncommercial split as useless, sees no benefit over a pure BSD license, argues the anti-GPL provision only burdens people combining GPL and OSSAL code, and urges using the BSD license instead.
timeline.point_zh: 认为商业/非商业的划分毫无用处,看不出该许可证比纯 BSD 有任何好处,反 GPL 条款只会给混用代码者添麻烦,建议直接使用 BSD。
timeline.point: Questions the commercial/noncommercial split as useless, sees no benefit over a pure BSD license, argues the anti-GPL provision only burdens people combining GPL and OSSAL code, and urges using the BSD license instead.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues that whether modifications are released as binary-only or under GPL, businesses cannot use them without restriction either way, making the OSSAL's GPL restriction no different from the existing BSD situation.
timeline.point_zh: 主张无论是以纯二进制形式还是 GPL 发布，企业在两种情况下都无法不受限制地使用修改，因此 OSSAL 的 GPL 限制与现有 BSD 情况并无不同。
timeline.point: Argues that whether modifications are released as binary-only or under GPL, businesses cannot use them without restriction either way, making the OSSAL's GPL restriction no different from the existing BSD situation.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues the OSSAL violates OSD #1 and #9 by restricting use of GPL software in conjunction with OSSAL software, noting the proposer's stated intent does not match the actual license terms.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 OSSAL 违反 OSD 第 1 条和第 9 条，因其限制 GPL 软件与 OSSAL 软件的联合使用，并指出提交者的意图与许可证实际条款不符。
timeline.point: Argues the OSSAL violates OSD #1 and #9 by restricting use of GPL software in conjunction with OSSAL software, noting the proposer's stated intent does not match the actual license terms.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Counters the Nokia/Checkpoint example by noting the Linux kernel allows proprietary drivers, explains BSD and copyleft serve different freedom goals for different communities, and notes old module versions remain available under their original license.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳 Nokia/Checkpoint 的例子，指出 Linux 内核允许专有驱动，解释 BSD 和 copyleft 为不同社区服务不同的自由目标，并指出旧模块版本仍按其原始许可证可用。
timeline.point: Counters the Nokia/Checkpoint example by noting the Linux kernel allows proprietary drivers, explains BSD and copyleft serve different freedom goals for different communities, and notes old module versions remain available under their original license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Reiterates that the OSSAL's only significant effect is prohibiting GPL forks—something the BSD license permits—and asks for a step-by-step explanation of why the same reasoning would not apply to the BSD license.
timeline.point_zh: 重申 OSSAL 的唯一显著效果是禁止 GPL 分叉,而 BSD 同样允许专有分叉,并要求对方逐步解释为何同样的分析不适用于 BSD。
timeline.point: Reiterates that the OSSAL's only significant effect is prohibiting GPL forks—something the BSD license permits—and asks for a step-by-step explanation of why the same reasoning would not apply to the BSD license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues that GPL ancestry can become fuzzy, so companies prefer code with a clearer lineage.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 GPL 会让代码来源变得模糊，因此公司更偏好来源更清晰的代码。
timeline.point: Argues that GPL ancestry can become fuzzy, so companies prefer code with a clearer lineage.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Calls the OSSAL a step in the right direction for small-shop developers whose needs are unmet by existing OSI-approved licenses, criticizes the community's 'just use the GPL' attitude, and hopes the OSI approves it in short order.
timeline.point_zh: 称 OSSAL 方向正确,切合未被现有 OSI 许可证满足的小型开发者需求,批评社区'用 GPL 就行'的态度,希望 OSI 尽快批准。
timeline.point: Calls the OSSAL a step in the right direction for small-shop developers whose needs are unmet by existing OSI-approved licenses, criticizes the community's 'just use the GPL' attitude, and hopes the OSI approves it in short order.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Rejects the claim that OSI is turning into a pro-GPL cheer section and says non-GPL views get flamed too.
timeline.point_zh: 否认 OSI 正在变成偏向 GPL 的阵营，并称非 GPL 观点也会被批评。
timeline.point: Rejects the claim that OSI is turning into a pro-GPL cheer section and says non-GPL views get flamed too.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says open-source code is unlikely to disappear for good and that most GPL violations are handled quietly.
timeline.point_zh: 认为开源代码通常不会真正消失，而且多数 GPL 违规会被低调解决。
timeline.point: Says open-source code is unlikely to disappear for good and that most GPL violations are handled quietly.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says BSD and Linux camps differ mainly in how they value coding freedom versus access to newer software.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 BSD 和 Linux 阵营主要差别在于更重视编程自由还是更重视较新的软件。
timeline.point: Says BSD and Linux camps differ mainly in how they value coding freedom versus access to newer software.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Recommends remedying the license's misleading ambiguities in the text itself, argues copyright law prevents other licenses from attaching to OSSAL-covered code, and concludes the provision—like Darren Reed's—cures a nonexistent problem and is a no-op.
timeline.point_zh: 建议在文本中直接修正误导性歧义,认为版权法已确保其他许可证无法'传染' OSSAL 代码,该条款像 Darren Reed 的一样在解决不存在的问题,形同虚设。
timeline.point: Recommends remedying the license's misleading ambiguities in the text itself, argues copyright law prevents other licenses from attaching to OSSAL-covered code, and concludes the provision—like Darren Reed's—cures a nonexistent problem and is a no-op.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Questions Ken Brown's citation and asks others what Bruce Perens actually said at the conference.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑 Ken Brown 的引述，并询问在场者 Bruce Perens 当时到底说了什么。
timeline.point: Questions Ken Brown's citation and asks others what Bruce Perens actually said at the conference.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Asks how the OSSAL helps anyone in a meaningful way and says that benefit was not explained.
timeline.point_zh: 询问 OSSAL 究竟如何真正帮助任何人，并指出对方没有解释清楚。
timeline.point: Asks how the OSSAL helps anyone in a meaningful way and says that benefit was not explained.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says he understands the complaint about GPL cheerleading but does not agree with it, and explains why small authors see OSI licenses as limiting.
timeline.point_zh: 表示理解对方对 GPL 偏向的抱怨，但并不认同，并解释小作者为何会觉得 OSI 许可证限制了自身商业模式。
timeline.point: Says he understands the complaint about GPL cheerleading but does not agree with it, and explains why small authors see OSI licenses as limiting.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues that the claim about OSI licenses is factually wrong and sounds like flamebait.
timeline.point_zh: 主张对 OSI 许可证的说法在事实上是错误的，而且像是在挑衅。
timeline.point: Argues that the claim about OSI licenses is factually wrong and sounds like flamebait.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says open-source licenses do not directly pay authors per user, so they do not fit the traditional software-sales model.
timeline.point_zh: 认为开源许可证无法按用户直接补偿作者，因此不适合传统的软件销售模式。
timeline.point: Says open-source licenses do not directly pay authors per user, so they do not fit the traditional software-sales model.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Makes a brief joking acknowledgment, then argues that GPL-cheerleading is really a misunderstanding caused by copyleft's complexity.
timeline.point_zh: 先用玩笑式语气回应，再主张所谓“偏向 GPL”其实多半源于对 copyleft 的误解和其复杂性。
timeline.point: Makes a brief joking acknowledgment, then argues that GPL-cheerleading is really a misunderstanding caused by copyleft's complexity.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Uses the message to accuse several people of IBM ties and says he would accept less money for his own research.
timeline.point_zh: 借此指责几位与 IBM 有关联，并表示自己愿意以更少资金支持研究。
timeline.point: Uses the message to accuse several people of IBM ties and says he would accept less money for his own research.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Defends OSSAL as OSD-compliant, saying it allows redistribution and coexistence with GPL code but blocks GPL mixing.
timeline.point_zh: 为 OSSAL 辩护，称其符合 OSD，允许再分发并可与 GPL 代码并行发布，但禁止与 GPL 混用。
timeline.point: Defends OSSAL as OSD-compliant, saying it allows redistribution and coexistence with GPL code but blocks GPL mixing.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues OSSAL, BSD, and MIT let developers reuse existing code and that OSSAL is meant to prevent duplicated effort.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 OSSAL、BSD 和 MIT 都让开发者复用现有代码，而 OSSAL 的目的就是避免重复劳动。
timeline.point: Argues OSSAL, BSD, and MIT let developers reuse existing code and that OSSAL is meant to prevent duplicated effort.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says the claim that OSI cheerleads for GPL is plainly wrong and that the earlier argument relied on hidden assumptions.
timeline.point_zh: 认为“OSI 在为 GPL 喝彩”这一说法明显错误，并指出前面的论证含有隐藏假设。
timeline.point: Says the claim that OSI cheerleads for GPL is plainly wrong and that the earlier argument relied on hidden assumptions.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Explains he wrote OSSAL, an MIT license with added baggage preventing copyleft modules, arguing that BSD/MIT licenses give businesses no quid pro quo and GPL modules make a language useless to commercial users.
timeline.point_zh: 解释其编写 OSSAL——附加条款防止 copyleft 模块的 MIT 改版——的理由：BSD/MIT 无互惠保障，GPL 模块对商业用户无用。
timeline.point: Explains he wrote OSSAL, an MIT license with added baggage preventing copyleft modules, arguing that BSD/MIT licenses give businesses no quid pro quo and GPL modules make a language useless to commercial users.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Insists the wording matches his intent, says the copyright issue is already understood, and asks for an offline explanation of the prior legal mistake.
timeline.point_zh: 坚持条文符合其本意，表示已明白版权问题，并要求提供关于此前法律错误的离线说明。
timeline.point: Insists the wording matches his intent, says the copyright issue is already understood, and asks for an offline explanation of the prior legal mistake.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Reiterates that GPL software raises costs for proprietary development and that under the OSSAL GPL contributions are worthless, so businesses would prefer a language whose modules are all under permissive licenses.
timeline.point_zh: 重申 GPL 软件抬高专有开发成本、OSSAL 下 GPL 贡献毫无价值，企业会偏好模块全部采用宽松许可的语言。
timeline.point: Reiterates that GPL software raises costs for proprietary development and that under the OSSAL GPL contributions are worthless, so businesses would prefer a language whose modules are all under permissive licenses.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues that BSD permits binary-only or GPL relicensing, but OSSAL is needed to keep modules on business-friendly terms and preserve reciprocity.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 BSD 允许二进制封闭发布或转为 GPL，而他需要 OSSAL 来确保模块以对商业友好的方式发布并形成互惠。
timeline.point: Argues that BSD permits binary-only or GPL relicensing, but OSSAL is needed to keep modules on business-friendly terms and preserve reciprocity.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues Linux is a business product and its advocates are IBM-paid capitalists, notes Perens conceded the GPL has commercial limitations, and claims BSD/MIT and other licenses date the GPL; questioning the GPL doesn't make one a conspirator.
timeline.point_zh: 称 Linux 是商业产品、其推动者受 IBM 资助，Perens 已承认 GPL 的商业局限，BSD/MIT 等许可使 GPL 过时；质疑 GPL 并非阴谋。
timeline.point: Argues Linux is a business product and its advocates are IBM-paid capitalists, notes Perens conceded the GPL has commercial limitations, and claims BSD/MIT and other licenses date the GPL; questioning the GPL doesn't make one a conspirator.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Tells Ken Brown to stop the offensive accusations and says publishing private mail is unacceptable.
timeline.point_zh: 要求 Ken Brown 停止冒犯性指控，并表示公开私人邮件不可接受。
timeline.point: Tells Ken Brown to stop the offensive accusations and says publishing private mail is unacceptable.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues users must always abide by a license's terms, and while OSSAL's intent to shield BSD-style code from GPL subsumption is clear, license-driven forks like bison/byacc are extremely rare in practice — taking no position on whether it is good.
timeline.point_zh: 认为必须遵守许可条款；OSSAL 防止 BSD 生态被 GPL 吸收的意图明确，但此类许可导致的分叉如 bison/byacc 极罕见，对其好坏不作表态。
timeline.point: Argues users must always abide by a license's terms, and while OSSAL's intent to shield BSD-style code from GPL subsumption is clear, license-driven forks like bison/byacc are extremely rare in practice — taking no position on whether it is good.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says interpreters are usually not GPL, questions OSSAL's reciprocity claims, and argues copyleft is what truly blocks proprietary improvements.
timeline.point_zh: 指出解释器通常并非 GPL，质疑 OSSAL 的互惠价值，并认为真正阻止专有改进的是 copyleft。
timeline.point: Says interpreters are usually not GPL, questions OSSAL's reciprocity claims, and argues copyleft is what truly blocks proprietary improvements.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Rejects the idea that software developers are merely doodling, defends support work as real commercial software, and says GPL software has served developers well.
timeline.point_zh: 反对把软件开发者说成是在“涂鸦”，为支撑专有业务的软件开发正名，并称 GPL 软件同样很好地服务了开发者。
timeline.point: Rejects the idea that software developers are merely doodling, defends support work as real commercial software, and says GPL software has served developers well.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Defends standards bodies and Linux as commerce-aiding industry standards, concedes the GPL has commercial limitations, but insists creators choose their own terms — those who dislike the GPL should use BSD-style licenses or simply not use Linux.
timeline.point_zh: 为标准组织和 Linux 作为产业标准辩护，承认 GPL 有商业局限，但坚持创作者自选条款；不喜欢 GPL 者可用 BSD 式许可或不使用 Linux。
timeline.point: Defends standards bodies and Linux as commerce-aiding industry standards, concedes the GPL has commercial limitations, but insists creators choose their own terms — those who dislike the GPL should use BSD-style licenses or simply not use Linux.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Asks why binary-only OSSAL terms would be friendly to other developers or users, and says GPL-averse authors would simply avoid releasing source.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑二进制封闭的 OSSAL 条款为何对其他开发者或用户友好，并认为不接受 GPL 的作者大可不发布源码。
timeline.point: Asks why binary-only OSSAL terms would be friendly to other developers or users, and says GPL-averse authors would simply avoid releasing source.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Criticizes Sean's misuse of 'business' to mean proprietary-software users, calls the GPL the real quid pro quo license, and accuses him of trolling rather than answering questions: 'If you just want a GPL-sucks license, say so.'
timeline.point_zh: 批评 Sean 滥用商业一词指代专有软件用户，指出 GPL 才是真正的 quid pro quo 许可，并指责其回避问题：若只想要反 GPL 许可就直说。
timeline.point: Criticizes Sean's misuse of 'business' to mean proprietary-software users, calls the GPL the real quid pro quo license, and accuses him of trolling rather than answering questions: 'If you just want a GPL-sucks license, say so.'

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Explains the language is a fast compiler for high-traffic needs, and defends the OSSAL as guaranteeing open source work stays usable by businesses without handicapping competitors — 'business' meaning widget makers shipping proprietary products.
timeline.point_zh: 解释该语言是满足高流量需求的高速编译器，并辩护 OSSAL 保证开源成果对企业可用且不妨碍竞争；业务指发布专有产品的 widget makers。
timeline.point: Explains the language is a fast compiler for high-traffic needs, and defends the OSSAL as guaranteeing open source work stays usable by businesses without handicapping competitors — 'business' meaning widget makers shipping proprietary products.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says binary-only OSSAL modules are the author's choice, but he still wants reciprocity among businesses and sees OSSAL as quid pro quo.
timeline.point_zh: 认为二进制封闭的 OSSAL 模块是作者自己的选择，但仍希望企业之间有互惠，并把 OSSAL 看作一种对价。
timeline.point: Says binary-only OSSAL modules are the author's choice, but he still wants reciprocity among businesses and sees OSSAL as quid pro quo.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Adopts the 'widget makers' terminology to avoid confusion, argues letting BSD code go closed-source is exactly what he wants, and says GPL and BSD/MIT don't fit his needs while the OSSAL — already improved by list scrutiny — does.
timeline.point_zh: 采纳 widget makers 术语以消除混淆，认为允许 BSD 代码转闭源正是其所愿；GPL 与 BSD/MIT 不合其需求，经列表审视改进的 OSSAL 合适。
timeline.point: Adopts the 'widget makers' terminology to avoid confusion, argues letting BSD code go closed-source is exactly what he wants, and says GPL and BSD/MIT don't fit his needs while the OSSAL — already improved by list scrutiny — does.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says interpreters are only one case, then argues that GPL tools still help proprietary businesses and that OSSAL mainly serves his own language work.
timeline.point_zh: 指出解释器只是其中一种情况，随后认为 GPL 工具同样能帮助专有业务，而 OSSAL 的价值主要在于适合他自己的语言项目。
timeline.point: Says interpreters are only one case, then argues that GPL tools still help proprietary businesses and that OSSAL mainly serves his own language work.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says GPL is long-lived but still practical in business, notes proprietary vendors contribute heavily to open source, and recommends approving OSSAL once ambiguities are fixed.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 GPL 影响长久但在商业上仍有实用性，指出专有软件公司也大量贡献开源，并建议在消除歧义后批准 OSSAL。
timeline.point: Says GPL is long-lived but still practical in business, notes proprietary vendors contribute heavily to open source, and recommends approving OSSAL once ambiguities are fixed.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues small shops need protection from commoditization, says GPL helps them, and questions whether OSSAL is better than BSD unless the customer wants fragmentation.
timeline.point_zh: 认为小型软件商需要防止商品化，指出 GPL 对他们有帮助，并质疑 OSSAL 除非客户想要碎片化，否则未必优于 BSD。
timeline.point: Argues small shops need protection from commoditization, says GPL helps them, and questions whether OSSAL is better than BSD unless the customer wants fragmentation.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says OSSAL users would still duplicate work, explains his reciprocity and cost-recovery rationale, and cites Linux adoption by big companies as a pro-GPL factor.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 OSSAL 用户仍会重复劳动，解释自己强调互惠与成本回收的原因，并以大公司采用 Linux 为 GPL 的正面例子。
timeline.point: Says OSSAL users would still duplicate work, explains his reciprocity and cost-recovery rationale, and cites Linux adoption by big companies as a pro-GPL factor.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues that the GPL is effectively a proprietary license from the FSF's perspective and objects to discrimination against the FSF.
timeline.point_zh: 主张从 FSF 的角度看 GPL 其实像专有许可证，并反对对 FSF 的歧视。
timeline.point: Argues that the GPL is effectively a proprietary license from the FSF's perspective and objects to discrimination against the FSF.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Suggests Sean may mainly want to prevent a competing GPL fork of his project and says that is at least a coherent concern.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 Sean 可能主要是想阻止项目出现有竞争力的 GPL 分支，并称这一担忧至少是自洽的。
timeline.point: Suggests Sean may mainly want to prevent a competing GPL fork of his project and says that is at least a coherent concern.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Asks what really distinguishes GPL from proprietary release for Sean's purposes and why BSD is good but GPL is bad.
timeline.point_zh: 询问在 Sean 的语境里 GPL 和专有发布究竟有何区别，以及为何 BSD 可以而 GPL 不行。
timeline.point: Asks what really distinguishes GPL from proprietary release for Sean's purposes and why BSD is good but GPL is bad.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says forks are rare, suggests a non-copyleft license is more appropriate if the concern is losing a GPL fork, and says the concern is at least comprehensible.
timeline.point_zh: 认为分叉很少见，若担心 GPL 分支被取代，更合适的做法是使用非 copyleft 许可，并表示这一担忧至少可以理解。
timeline.point: Says forks are rare, suggests a non-copyleft license is more appropriate if the concern is losing a GPL fork, and says the concern is at least comprehensible.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Notes that the bison/byacc fork did change licensing conditions, contradicting the claim that no successful fork has done so.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 bison/byacc 分支确实改变了许可条件，反驳“没有成功分支改变过许可”的说法。
timeline.point: Notes that the bison/byacc fork did change licensing conditions, contradicting the claim that no successful fork has done so.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Suggests the EU DataGrid Software License would achieve the same anti-GPL effect while making forks less likely.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 EU DataGrid 软件许可证也能达到同样的反 GPL 效果，而且更不容易引发分叉。
timeline.point: Suggests the EU DataGrid Software License would achieve the same anti-GPL effect while making forks less likely.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Defends OSSAL as acceptable, questions the approval-process remark, and jokes that non-GPL conclusions are treated as flawed.
timeline.point_zh: 为 OSSAL 辩护，质疑对方是否参与审批流程，并讽刺说只要不是 GPL 的结论就会被视为论证有缺陷。
timeline.point: Defends OSSAL as acceptable, questions the approval-process remark, and jokes that non-GPL conclusions are treated as flawed.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues GPL is unattractive to widget manufacturers, while OSSAL provides dependable components and avoids a semantics fight over the word business.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 GPL 对小部件制造商没有吸引力，而 OSSAL 能提供可依赖的组件；同时反对围绕“business”一词做语义争论。
timeline.point: Argues GPL is unattractive to widget manufacturers, while OSSAL provides dependable components and avoids a semantics fight over the word business.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says reducing duplication matters, but being able to reuse code in products matters more; he wants contributions from other widget makers and wants them to remain usable in proprietary products.
timeline.point_zh: 表示他重视减少重复劳动，但更重视把代码用于产品；他希望得到其他小部件制造商的贡献，并且这些贡献要能用于专有产品。
timeline.point: Says reducing duplication matters, but being able to reuse code in products matters more; he wants contributions from other widget makers and wants them to remain usable in proprietary products.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Clarifies he is only speaking as a list member, then notes his own software was dual-licensed under GPL because AFL’s patent clause made it GPL-incompatible.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清自己只是以该邮件列表成员身份发言，并说明他自己的软件因 AFL 的专利条款与 GPL 不兼容而采用了双重许可。
timeline.point: Clarifies he is only speaking as a list member, then notes his own software was dual-licensed under GPL because AFL’s patent clause made it GPL-incompatible.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues OSSAL lets widget makers use code in proprietary products while keeping public module work reusable, and says GPL use would be an ethical tease.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 OSSAL 让小部件制造商能够在专有产品中使用代码，同时让公共模块工作保持可复用；并认为 GPL 的做法像是在故意吊胃口。
timeline.point: Argues OSSAL lets widget makers use code in proprietary products while keeping public module work reusable, and says GPL use would be an ethical tease.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges the fork risk but says his larger goal is keeping code usable to widget manufacturers.
timeline.point_zh: 承认分叉风险是个顾虑，但表示更重要的目标是确保代码对小部件制造商始终可用。
timeline.point: Acknowledges the fork risk but says his larger goal is keeping code usable to widget manufacturers.
