timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says GPL-derived changes are only available under GPL and uses that as the reason GPL is bad relative to proprietary reuse.
timeline.point_zh: 指出由 GPL 产品作者对 BSD 代码所做的修改只能在 GPL 下可用，并据此认为 GPL 相对专有复用是有问题的。
timeline.point: Says GPL-derived changes are only available under GPL and uses that as the reason GPL is bad relative to proprietary reuse.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges there was no special OSI power involved and asks what the AFL patent poison pill is.
timeline.point_zh: 表示自己不知道对方在 OSI 审核中是否有特殊权力，并询问 AFL 的专利毒丸条款是什么意思。
timeline.point: Acknowledges there was no special OSI power involved and asks what the AFL patent poison pill is.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Suggests a community-style license that keeps modifications public while giving Sean special licensing freedom, but warns it may not pass OSI because it discriminates.
timeline.point_zh: 建议采用一种社区式许可证，让修改保持公开，同时赋予 Sean 特殊许可自由，但提醒这类许可证可能因歧视而无法通过 OSI 认证。
timeline.point: Suggests a community-style license that keeps modifications public while giving Sean special licensing freedom, but warns it may not pass OSI because it discriminates.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Explains that AFL includes a patent retaliation clause and that the FSF treats it as GPL-incompatible.
timeline.point_zh: 解释 AFL 包含专利反制条款，因此 FSF 将其视为与 GPL 不兼容。
timeline.point: Explains that AFL includes a patent retaliation clause and that the FSF treats it as GPL-incompatible.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues a unilateral waiver of GPL incompatibility probably would not work, because the GPL licensor would still control compatibility.
timeline.point_zh: 认为单方面声明放弃与 GPL 的不兼容性大概行不通，因为 GPL 的许可方仍然掌握兼容性的控制权。
timeline.point: Argues a unilateral waiver of GPL incompatibility probably would not work, because the GPL licensor would still control compatibility.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Explains that AFL and related licenses can trigger a broad patent poison pill, and notes that GPL has an implicit patent poison pill through its further-restrictions rule.
timeline.point_zh: 说明 AFL 及相关许可证的专利毒丸影响范围更广，并指出 GPL 也通过“附加限制”规则隐含了专利毒丸。
timeline.point: Explains that AFL and related licenses can trigger a broad patent poison pill, and notes that GPL has an implicit patent poison pill through its further-restrictions rule.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues the OSSAL is not a quid pro quo license: changes can be relicensed under terms barring the original author from using them, so it fails to protect against the very problem it targets — it is merely a 'GPL sucks' license.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 OSSAL 并非对等互惠许可证：修改可被以排斥原作者的条款再授权，无法防止它针对的问题——它只是'讨厌GPL'的许可证。
timeline.point: Argues the OSSAL is not a quid pro quo license: changes can be relicensed under terms barring the original author from using them, so it fails to protect against the very problem it targets — it is merely a 'GPL sucks' license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says OSSAL is more distributed than MPL and therefore more appealing than MPL.
timeline.point_zh: 表示 OSSAL 比 MPL 更分散，因此比 MPL 更合他的偏好。
timeline.point: Says OSSAL is more distributed than MPL and therefore more appealing than MPL.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues OSSAL keeps non-core changes available to other widget makers by preventing GPL relicensing.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 OSSAL 通过阻止再许可为 GPL，使非核心修改继续对其他小部件制造商可用。
timeline.point: Argues OSSAL keeps non-core changes available to other widget makers by preventing GPL relicensing.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Concerned that clause 4, barring use with source-disclosure licenses like the GPL, makes it an 'anti-GPL' license; argues 'don't use that license' wording discriminates, unlike legitimate reciprocity, and asks whether such provisions violate the OSD.
timeline.point_zh: 担心第4条禁止与GPL等要求公开源码的许可证同用，使其成为'反GPL'许可证；认为'不得使用那种许可证'式措辞构成歧视，不同于正当的互惠条款，并询问此类条款是否违反OSD。
timeline.point: Concerned that clause 4, barring use with source-disclosure licenses like the GPL, makes it an 'anti-GPL' license; argues 'don't use that license' wording discriminates, unlike legitimate reciprocity, and asks whether such provisions violate the OSD.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says the GPL reference made the issue blow up, asks which OSD term is violated, and asks how to rephrase the restriction without losing its intent.
timeline.point_zh: 表示是 GPL 的举例让争论升级，询问究竟违反了 OSD 哪一条，并寻求在不丢失原意的前提下改写条款的方法。
timeline.point: Says the GPL reference made the issue blow up, asks which OSD term is violated, and asks how to rephrase the restriction without losing its intent.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Challenges Sean’s distinction between OSSAL and GPL contributions by asking why GPL donations should be treated differently from proprietary ones.
timeline.point_zh: 通过提问指出：既然专有许可的贡献可以拒绝，为什么 GPL 的贡献就要被区别对待。
timeline.point: Challenges Sean’s distinction between OSSAL and GPL contributions by asking why GPL donations should be treated differently from proprietary ones.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues the “don’t use that license” distinction is meaningless and that GPL itself discriminates against proprietary software.
timeline.point_zh: 认为“不要使用那个许可证”与其他许可之间并无本质区别，并指出 GPL 本身也在歧视专有软件作者。
timeline.point: Argues the “don’t use that license” distinction is meaningless and that GPL itself discriminates against proprietary software.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues the OSSAL's ban on linking to GPL-type software is discriminatory, since writing an interface to a GPL'ed program is not creating a derivative work; if this clause clears the OSD, then the OSD itself should be amended.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 OSSAL 禁止与GPL类软件链接具有歧视性，因为为GPL程序编写接口不构成衍生作品；若此条款能通过OSD，则应修改的正是OSD本身。
timeline.point: Argues the OSSAL's ban on linking to GPL-type software is discriminatory, since writing an interface to a GPL'ed program is not creating a derivative work; if this clause clears the OSD, then the OSD itself should be amended.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Disagrees that the OSSAL prevents a GPL takeover: modifiers have incentives to pick the GPL, which would win out as the popular license, and the OSSAL may instead push improvements into proprietary code; suggests a dual-distribution rewording as less inflammatory.
timeline.point_zh: 不认同 OSSAL 能阻止GPL主导：修改者有动机选择GPL，更流行的许可证终将胜出；OSSAL 反而可能促使改进流入专有代码，并建议改为要求双重发布的措辞以减少对抗性。
timeline.point: Disagrees that the OSSAL prevents a GPL takeover: modifiers have incentives to pick the GPL, which would win out as the popular license, and the OSSAL may instead push improvements into proprietary code; suggests a dual-distribution rewording as less inflammatory.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: States that OSSAL does not guarantee business-friendly terms and therefore fails to achieve Sean’s goal.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 OSSAL 并不能保证软件始终以对商业友好的条款发布，因此没有实现 Sean 的目标。
timeline.point: States that OSSAL does not guarantee business-friendly terms and therefore fails to achieve Sean’s goal.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Criticizes the GPL as legally troubled and says license proliferation and conflicting terms are a real problem.
timeline.point_zh: 批评 GPL 在法律上有问题，并指出许可证泛滥与条款冲突确实是个问题。
timeline.point: Criticizes the GPL as legally troubled and says license proliferation and conflicting terms are a real problem.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Explains that an open-source license could require payment to the copyright holder upon receipt, and notes some companies tolerate piracy because it can help them.
timeline.point_zh: 解释说开源许可证可以要求从版权持有人处获取软件时支付费用，并指出有些公司会容忍“盗版”，因为这对它们也有好处。
timeline.point: Explains that an open-source license could require payment to the copyright holder upon receipt, and notes some companies tolerate piracy because it can help them.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Likes David Presotto’s proposed wording and says it should apply only to derivative works, not unchanged code.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 David Presotto 提出的措辞很巧妙，并建议只把它用于衍生作品，而不是未修改的代码。
timeline.point: Likes David Presotto’s proposed wording and says it should apply only to derivative works, not unchanged code.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Challenges Sean for treating GPL as worse than proprietary licensing and asks why OSSAL favors one proprietary style over another.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑 Sean 把 GPL 看得比专有许可更糟，并询问为什么 OSSAL 会偏向某一种专有许可而排斥另一种。
timeline.point: Challenges Sean for treating GPL as worse than proprietary licensing and asks why OSSAL favors one proprietary style over another.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says OSSAL does not prevent the problem Sean worries about and that code can still end up GPL-licensed; questions practical examples.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 OSSAL 并不能阻止 Sean 担心的问题，代码仍然可能最终以 GPL 形式出现，并追问现实中是否真有这样的公司。
timeline.point: Says OSSAL does not prevent the problem Sean worries about and that code can still end up GPL-licensed; questions practical examples.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Counters that a copyright holder can dual-license and release new modules of OSSAL code under the GPL, so the OSSAL does not prevent GPL capture; notes nobody in practice releases GPL versions of BSD code, and the OSSAL is easier to exploit than the GPL.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳称版权持有者可通过双重许可将 OSSAL 代码的新模块以GPL发布，因此 OSSAL 无法防止被GPL占据；实践中无人为BSD代码发布GPL版本，而 OSSAL 比 GPL 更易被利用。
timeline.point: Counters that a copyright holder can dual-license and release new modules of OSSAL code under the GPL, so the OSSAL does not prevent GPL capture; notes nobody in practice releases GPL versions of BSD code, and the OSSAL is easier to exploit than the GPL.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Questions whether the word use in the Microsoft-style restriction can be defined in a way that does not also exclude the GPL.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑能否把这里的“use”定义得足够精确，而不会顺带把 GPL 也排除掉。
timeline.point: Questions whether the word use in the Microsoft-style restriction can be defined in a way that does not also exclude the GPL.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues 'people who use the GPL' is not a 'group' or 'field of endeavor' under OSD clauses 4 and 5, and the license is anti-GPL just as the GPL is anti-everything-non-GPL; sees no OSD violation and calls it an interesting test case.
timeline.point_zh: 认为'使用GPL的人群'不属于OSD第4、5条的'群体'或'领域'，该许可证反GPL正如 GPL 反一切非GPL许可证；未发现其违反OSD，视其为有趣的测试案例。
timeline.point: Argues 'people who use the GPL' is not a 'group' or 'field of endeavor' under OSD clauses 4 and 5, and the license is anti-GPL just as the GPL is anti-everything-non-GPL; sees no OSD violation and calls it an interesting test case.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Clarifies his point about payment per use rather than download fees, and says some people think software users should pay authors.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清自己说的是按使用付费，而不是下载收费，并指出有些人确实认为软件使用者应该向作者付费。
timeline.point: Clarifies his point about payment per use rather than download fees, and says some people think software users should pay authors.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Apologizes for the earlier misunderstanding and says he was not clear enough.
timeline.point_zh: 为前面的误解道歉，并表示自己表达得不够清楚。
timeline.point: Apologizes for the earlier misunderstanding and says he was not clear enough.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says the meaning of should depends on enforcement and declines to continue an off-topic digression.
timeline.point_zh: 表示 should 的含义取决于是否通过强制执行，并拒绝继续偏题讨论。
timeline.point: Says the meaning of should depends on enforcement and declines to continue an off-topic digression.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Pushes back on the idea that users should pay for software value, warning that such a view belongs to proprietary software.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳“用户应为软件价值付费”的观点，并提醒这种想法更接近专有软件立场。
timeline.point: Pushes back on the idea that users should pay for software value, warning that such a view belongs to proprietary software.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Explains the OSSAL aims to let widget makers cut costs by ensuring changes flow back under OSSAL terms; a GPL patch is as unusable as no patch, since GPL terms block use in products — the motivation behind the OSSAL's stance against the GPL.
timeline.point_zh: 解释 OSSAL 旨在让设备厂商降低成本、确保修改以 OSSAL 条款回流；GPL补丁如同不可用的补丁，因 GPL 条款阻止在产品中使用——这正是 OSSAL 反GPL立场的动机。
timeline.point: Explains the OSSAL aims to let widget makers cut costs by ensuring changes flow back under OSSAL terms; a GPL patch is as unusable as no patch, since GPL terms block use in products — the motivation behind the OSSAL's stance against the GPL.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues GPL dependence blocks widget makers and that OSSAL is a counterreaction to GPL fragmentation.
timeline.point_zh: 认为依赖 GPL 会阻碍小部件制造商，因此 OSSAL 是对 GPL 造成碎片化的反作用。
timeline.point: Argues GPL dependence blocks widget makers and that OSSAL is a counterreaction to GPL fragmentation.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says OSSAL targets the wrong thing and recommends the EU Datagrid license instead.
timeline.point_zh: 表示 OSSAL 针对错了对象，并建议改用 EU Datagrid 许可证。
timeline.point: Says OSSAL targets the wrong thing and recommends the EU Datagrid license instead.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Predicts BSD/OSSAL software will persist as long as markets exist and defends the anti-GPL stance: the GPL excludes widget makers from the open source movement; rejects softening the clauses as diluting his intent and will draft another version.
timeline.point_zh: 预言只要市场存在 BSD/OSSAL 软件就会存续，并为其反GPL立场辩护：GPL 将设备厂商排除在开源运动之外；认为软化措辞会稀释本意，将再拟新版本。
timeline.point: Predicts BSD/OSSAL software will persist as long as markets exist and defends the anti-GPL stance: the GPL excludes widget makers from the open source movement; rejects softening the clauses as diluting his intent and will draft another version.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says business contributors can benefit the community while still making money, and states his real goal is to block GPLed contributions and GPL forks while allowing only OSSA/BSD/MIT-like terms.
timeline.point_zh: 认为做生意的贡献者也可以在赚钱的同时回馈社区；并明确表示他的真实目标是阻止 GPL 贡献和 GPL 分叉，只允许 OSSA/BSD/MIT 类条款。
timeline.point: Says business contributors can benefit the community while still making money, and states his real goal is to block GPLed contributions and GPL forks while allowing only OSSA/BSD/MIT-like terms.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues that GPL-licensed code is worse than proprietary code because it blocks widget makers from reusing software and contributing changes back.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 GPL 许可证下的代码比专有许可更糟，因为它阻碍小部件厂商复用软件并把改动回馈社区。
timeline.point: Argues that GPL-licensed code is worse than proprietary code because it blocks widget makers from reusing software and contributing changes back.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says the GPL-versus-proprietary distinction should be left to market forces rather than extra license language.
timeline.point_zh: 表示 GPL 与专有许可之间的差异应交给市场力量，而不是再加法律条款来处理。
timeline.point: Says the GPL-versus-proprietary distinction should be left to market forces rather than extra license language.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Notes GPL-style inheritive-license clauses would prevent the discussed problem but are reprehensible tactics; since the OSSAL assumes reciprocity among its community, is unsure this should be solved through license restrictions and will keep thinking it over.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 GPL 式继承条款虽能防止该问题，却属于可鄙手段；因 OSSAL 假设社区互惠，不确定该问题是否应通过许可限制解决，仍需再想想。
timeline.point: Notes GPL-style inheritive-license clauses would prevent the discussed problem but are reprehensible tactics; since the OSSAL assumes reciprocity among its community, is unsure this should be solved through license restrictions and will keep thinking it over.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues many creators strongly believe in per-copy compensation, a view open source neither accommodates nor needs to; most people eventually 'get it', but some remain passionate about fee-per-copy fairness.
timeline.point_zh: 认为许多创作者坚信按副本收费的公平性，开源不接纳也不必接纳这种诉求；多数人最终会理解，但有些人始终执著于按副本收费。
timeline.point: Argues many creators strongly believe in per-copy compensation, a view open source neither accommodates nor needs to; most people eventually 'get it', but some remain passionate about fee-per-copy fairness.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that OSI has approved many GPL-incompatible licenses, and distinguishes five separate criticisms of the license — moral, pointless, strategic, ineffective, and duplicative — encouraging the author to address them constructively.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清 OSI 曾批准过多个与 GPL 不兼容的许可，并梳理了针对该许可的五种不同批评（道德、无意义、策略、无效、重复），鼓励作者建设性地回应。
timeline.point: Clarifies that OSI has approved many GPL-incompatible licenses, and distinguishes five separate criticisms of the license — moral, pointless, strategic, ineffective, and duplicative — encouraging the author to address them constructively.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says he is specifically biased against software that cannot be used in products, dislikes the GPL, and is still evaluating the EU DataGrid license.
timeline.point_zh: 表示他明确反感无法用于产品的软件，尤其不喜欢 GPL，但仍在评估 EU DataGrid 许可。
timeline.point: Says he is specifically biased against software that cannot be used in products, dislikes the GPL, and is still evaluating the EU DataGrid license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: States that the license is open source, that anti-GPL licenses do not violate the OSD, and that the OSD can be changed if the board disagrees.
timeline.point_zh: 表示该许可证属于开源，反 GPL 的许可证并不违反 OSD；如果 OSI 不认同，也可以修改 OSD。
timeline.point: States that the license is open source, that anti-GPL licenses do not violate the OSD, and that the OSD can be changed if the board disagrees.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Argues the OSSAL's implicit claim of moral high ground fails, since it bars GPL forks while BSD permits similar bait-and-switch; suggests ratification should rest only on OSD compliance, and personally would never use the license.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 OSSAL 自居道德高地站不住脚——它禁止 GPL 分叉却接受 BSD 式的 bait and switch；主张批准只看 OSD 合规性，且自己绝不会使用该许可。
timeline.point: Argues the OSSAL's implicit claim of moral high ground fails, since it bars GPL forks while BSD permits similar bait-and-switch; suggests ratification should rest only on OSD compliance, and personally would never use the license.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Agrees that companies may close their own derivatives, says market choice should decide the outcome, and rejects being cast as politically right-wing.
timeline.point_zh: 同意公司可以闭源自己的衍生版本，认为结果应由市场选择决定，并拒绝被贴上右翼政治标签。
timeline.point: Agrees that companies may close their own derivatives, says market choice should decide the outcome, and rejects being cast as politically right-wing.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Apologizes for mixing up who said what in the thread.
timeline.point_zh: 为自己混淆了讨论中各人的发言而道歉。
timeline.point: Apologizes for mixing up who said what in the thread.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Separates the debate into ideological and practical issues, says OSSAL still does not fully solve the problem, and notes concern that EU DataGrid code can depend on GPL bits.
timeline.point_zh: 把争论分成意识形态与实际问题两部分，认为 OSSAL 仍未完全解决问题，并指出 EU DataGrid 代码可能依赖 GPL 组件。
timeline.point: Separates the debate into ideological and practical issues, says OSSAL still does not fully solve the problem, and notes concern that EU DataGrid code can depend on GPL bits.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says he was only reacting to the word “usurped,” agrees with the free-enterprise framing, and is not taking a broader stance on the licensing dispute.
timeline.point_zh: 表示自己只是对“usurped”这个词作出反应，同意自由市场的表述，并未就许可证争议本身表态。
timeline.point: Says he was only reacting to the word “usurped,” agrees with the free-enterprise framing, and is not taking a broader stance on the licensing dispute.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Rebuts claims that approving GPL-conflicting licenses constitutes discrimination, notes the copyleft-conversion problem is inherently non-existent, and judges the OSSAL OSD-compliant even though its squirrelly wording badly needs a good editor.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳'批准与 GPL 冲突的许可即属歧视'之说，指出 copyleft 转换问题本不存在，并认为 OSSAL 符合 OSD，只是拗口的措辞亟需好好编辑。
timeline.point: Rebuts claims that approving GPL-conflicting licenses constitutes discrimination, notes the copyleft-conversion problem is inherently non-existent, and judges the OSSAL OSD-compliant even though its squirrelly wording badly needs a good editor.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says OSI has already approved many GPL-incompatible licenses and that the real question is whether the OSD itself should be changed.
timeline.point_zh: 表示 OSI 早已批准过许多与 GPL 不兼容的许可证，真正的问题是 OSD 本身是否需要修改。
timeline.point: Says OSI has already approved many GPL-incompatible licenses and that the real question is whether the OSD itself should be changed.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Source Software Alliance License
timeline.snippet: Says a different clause might have been less inflammatory, but he dislikes restrictions in both GPL and OSSAL and still regards both as open source.
timeline.point_zh: 表示如果换一种条款可能没那么刺激，但他同样不喜欢 GPL 和 OSSAL 里的限制，并仍把两者都视为开源。
timeline.point: Says a different clause might have been less inflammatory, but he dislikes restrictions in both GPL and OSSAL and still regards both as open source.

submissions.rejection_reason: Never approved. BSD-derivative with added attribution and notification requirements that were seen as overly restrictive.

submissions.name: BXAPL

curated_rwp.rejection_reason: Never approved. License terms violated OSD.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Submits the Bixoft Public License (BXAPL) for review, explaining no OSI-approved license meets criteria like distinguishing programming tools and treating copyrights and patents separately, answering the standard questions, and inviting discussion and comments.
timeline.point_zh: 提交 Bixoft Public License(BXAPL)供审查,称现有 OSI 许可证均不满足区分编程工具、分别处理版权与专利等标准,并回答标准问题、欢迎讨论。
timeline.point: Submits the Bixoft Public License (BXAPL) for review, explaining no OSI-approved license meets criteria like distinguishing programming tools and treating copyrights and patents separately, answering the standard questions, and inviting discussion and comments.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Believes the BXAPL meets the Open Source Definition but raises concerns about the patent provisions in paragraph 16 potentially being unenforceable.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 BXAPL 符合开放源代码定义，但对第 16 条专利条款可能无法执行提出了关切。
timeline.point: Believes the BXAPL meets the Open Source Definition but raises concerns about the patent provisions in paragraph 16 potentially being unenforceable.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that paragraph 16 addresses how the license terminates between patent and copyright holders, not payment for patent use.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清第 16 条涉及的是专利权人与版权持有人之间的许可终止方式，而非专利使用费。
timeline.point: Clarifies that paragraph 16 addresses how the license terminates between patent and copyright holders, not payment for patent use.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Recommends against OSI approval, arguing the license resembles a EULA and its self-declared Programming Tool distinction is ripe for abuse.
timeline.point_zh: 建议不予 OSI 批准，认为该许可证类似终端用户许可协议，且其自定义的编程工具分类容易被滥用。
timeline.point: Recommends against OSI approval, arguing the license resembles a EULA and its self-declared Programming Tool distinction is ripe for abuse.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Defends the BXAPL against review criticism, conceding a couple of terms need rewording while arguing the Programming Tool designation imposes no burden and clarifying the Contributor/Distributor definitions and the distribution clause's scope.
timeline.point_zh: 为 BXAPL 辩护:承认个别措辞需修改,但认为 Programming Tool 标注机制并无负担,并澄清 Contributor/Distributor 定义及分发条款的范围。
timeline.point: Defends the BXAPL against review criticism, conceding a couple of terms need rewording while arguing the Programming Tool designation imposes no burden and clarifying the Contributor/Distributor definitions and the distribution clause's scope.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Explains the Dependent Software concept — software using but not modifying Programming Tools — and defends the patent-dispute royalty provision as borrowed from CPL/IBMPL, meant to stop patent holders using the software while litigating.
timeline.point_zh: 解释 Dependent Software(使用但不修改编程工具的软件)概念,并以 CPL/IBMPL 为先例为专利争议版税条款辩护,旨在阻止专利权人诉讼期间免费使用软件。
timeline.point: Explains the Dependent Software concept — software using but not modifying Programming Tools — and defends the patent-dispute royalty provision as borrowed from CPL/IBMPL, meant to stop patent holders using the software while litigating.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Rebuffs BXAPL criticisms: denies it is a EULA, explains the per-item Programming Tool designation resulted from failing to craft a general one, sees no abuse loophole, and asks where par. 12 is inconsistent.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳对 BXAPL 的批评:否认其为 EULA,解释因无法给出通用表述而采用逐项标注 Programming Tool,认为无滥用漏洞,并请指出第 12 段的不一致之处。
timeline.point: Rebuffs BXAPL criticisms: denies it is a EULA, explains the per-item Programming Tool designation resulted from failing to craft a general one, sees no abuse loophole, and asks where par. 12 is inconsistent.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Points out that the Contributor definition implies every Distributor is a Contributor, contradicting Steve Lhomme's earlier claim.
timeline.point_zh: 指出贡献者定义暗示每位分发者都是贡献者，这与 Steve Lhomme 此前的说法相矛盾。
timeline.point: Points out that the Contributor definition implies every Distributor is a Contributor, contradicting Steve Lhomme's earlier claim.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Raises concerns about how trademark marks embedded in software interact with distribution requirements and questions whether users can remove them.
timeline.point_zh: 对软件中嵌入的商标与分发要求之间的关系提出关切，并质疑用户是否可以移除这些商标。
timeline.point: Raises concerns about how trademark marks embedded in software interact with distribution requirements and questions whether users can remove them.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Questions whether the broad User definition could create unintended patent-related obligations when someone receives software to inspect for infringement.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑过于宽泛的用户定义是否会在有人收到软件以检查侵权时产生意外的专利相关义务。
timeline.point: Questions whether the broad User definition could create unintended patent-related obligations when someone receives software to inspect for infringement.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Argues the Source Code definition may inadvertently include compilers and linkers, creating ambiguity about what must be distributed.
timeline.point_zh: 认为源代码定义可能无意中包含了编译器和链接器，导致必须分发的内容存在歧义。
timeline.point: Argues the Source Code definition may inadvertently include compilers and linkers, creating ambiguity about what must be distributed.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that a Distributor only becomes a Contributor when it supplies modifications to the copyright holder.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清分发者仅在向版权持有人提供修改时才成为贡献者。
timeline.point: Clarifies that a Distributor only becomes a Contributor when it supplies modifications to the copyright holder.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges the intent behind paragraph 16 but argues it would likely be ruled unenforceable in court, becoming useless for protecting open-source developers.
timeline.point_zh: 承认第 16 条的初衷，但认为其在法庭上很可能被判无法执行，对保护开源开发者毫无用处。
timeline.point: Acknowledges the intent behind paragraph 16 but argues it would likely be ruled unenforceable in court, becoming useless for protecting open-source developers.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that Distributors are by definition always Contributors, but Contributors are not always Distributors.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清分发者按定义始终是贡献者，但贡献者并不总是分发者。
timeline.point: Clarifies that Distributors are by definition always Contributors, but Contributors are not always Distributors.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Argues that displaying software output does not constitute trademark use and that redistribution remains permitted, but removing marks is not allowed without permission.
timeline.point_zh: 认为展示软件输出不构成商标使用，重新分发仍然被允许，但未经许可不得移除标识。
timeline.point: Argues that displaying software output does not constitute trademark use and that redistribution remains permitted, but removing marks is not allowed without permission.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Apologizes for off-list replies and responds to BXAPL critique: the patent clause obliges a Patent Holder only if it uses the Software, code inspection likely is not 'use', and the User definition needs narrowing — wording suggestions welcome.
timeline.point_zh: 为未抄送列表致歉并回应批评:专利条款仅在 Patent Holder 使用软件时才触发付费,检查代码不算"使用",同意收窄 User 定义并征求措辞建议。
timeline.point: Apologizes for off-list replies and responds to BXAPL critique: the patent clause obliges a Patent Holder only if it uses the Software, code inspection likely is not 'use', and the User definition needs narrowing — wording suggestions welcome.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges the Source Code definition inadvertently includes compilers and linkers, proposes a fix excluding commonly available tools, and asks for feedback.
timeline.point_zh: 承认源代码定义无意中包含了编译器和链接器，提出排除常用工具的修正方案，并征求反馈意见。
timeline.point: Acknowledges the Source Code definition inadvertently includes compilers and linkers, proposes a fix excluding commonly available tools, and asks for feedback.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Questions why the two license authors disagree on the Distributor-Contributor relationship.
timeline.point_zh: 质问两位许可证作者为何在分发者-贡献者关系上存在分歧。
timeline.point: Questions why the two license authors disagree on the Distributor-Contributor relationship.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges the disagreement with Abe on the Distributor-Contributor relationship and proposes removing the link between them.
timeline.point_zh: 承认与 Abe 在分发者-贡献者关系上存在分歧，并提议取消两者之间的关联。
timeline.point: Acknowledges the disagreement with Abe on the Distributor-Contributor relationship and proposes removing the link between them.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Publishes his private exchange with Nathan Kelley, agreeing to fix Item 10's Modification wording while defending Item 16 as a knowingly 'retaliatory' royalty clause serving as negotiation leverage, not a device to hamper patent enforcement.
timeline.point_zh: 公布与 Nathan Kelley 的私下讨论,同意修正第 10 条的 Modification 措辞,但为第 16 条"报复性"版税条款辩护,称其为谈判筹码而非妨碍专利行使。
timeline.point: Publishes his private exchange with Nathan Kelley, agreeing to fix Item 10's Modification wording while defending Item 16 as a knowingly 'retaliatory' royalty clause serving as negotiation leverage, not a device to hamper patent enforcement.

timeline.subject: Approval request for BXAPL
timeline.snippet: Concedes the BXAPL's Contributor/Distributor definitions are prone to misunderstanding, explains why Distributors were folded into Contributor, and accepts the definitions likely need untangling, inviting better suggestions.
timeline.point_zh: 承认 BXAPL 的 Contributor/Distributor 定义易生误解,解释将 Distributor 并入 Contributor 的原因,认为定义需重新梳理,并征求更好建议。
timeline.point: Concedes the BXAPL's Contributor/Distributor definitions are prone to misunderstanding, explains why Distributors were folded into Contributor, and accepts the definitions likely need untangling, inviting better suggestions.

submissions.rejection_reason: Never approved. License terms violated OSD.

submissions.name: APOSSL (Anti-Piracy Open Source Software License)

curated_rwp.rejection_reason: Never approved. The license's anti-piracy focus imposed restrictions inconsistent with the OSD.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Submits APOSSL (A Pronoic Open Source Software Licence) 1.0 for OSI approval — a largely BSD-style license with unusual clauses requiring derived products to be described as "pronoic" while restricting use of the Pronoic name.
timeline.point_zh: 提交 APOSSL（A Pronoic Open Source Software Licence）1.0 供 OSI 审批——该许可证大体为 BSD 风格，但包含要求衍生产品被描述为"pronoic"并限制使用 Pronoic 名称的特殊条款。
timeline.point: Submits APOSSL (A Pronoic Open Source Software Licence) 1.0 for OSI approval — a largely BSD-style license with unusual clauses requiring derived products to be described as "pronoic" while restricting use of the Pronoic name.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Argues that the license fails the OSD because clause 4 requires promotion of derivatives and clause 5 requires written permission for naming, and asserts that the OSI should not approve it.
timeline.point_zh: 认为该许可证因第4条强制推广衍生作品、第5条要求书面许可命名而违反 OSD，不应获批准。
timeline.point: Argues that the license fails the OSD because clause 4 requires promotion of derivatives and clause 5 requires written permission for naming, and asserts that the OSI should not approve it.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Counters that pronoic is a descriptive word rather than a name, that clauses 4 and 5 do not conflict with the OSD, and that the license can stand on its own.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳对方解读，主张 pronoic 是描述性词汇而非名称，第4、5条不构成 OSD 冲突，许可证可独立成立。
timeline.point: Counters that pronoic is a descriptive word rather than a name, that clauses 4 and 5 do not conflict with the OSD, and that the license can stand on its own.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Argues that clause 4's literal meaning compels endorsement and promotion of derivative products, contrary to the other party's interpretation, and asks for others' opinions.
timeline.point_zh: 认为第4条字面意为强制要求推广衍生作品，与对方解读相左，并征求他人意见。
timeline.point: Argues that clause 4's literal meaning compels endorsement and promotion of derivative products, contrary to the other party's interpretation, and asks for others' opinions.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Emphasizes that legal documents should not contain undefined invented words, that capitalization differences are a thin basis for legal arguments, and that requiring written permission is itself an OSD conflict.
timeline.point_zh: 强调法律文件不应含未定义生造词，大小写区分难以支撑法律论点，要求书面许可本身就违反 OSD。
timeline.point: Emphasizes that legal documents should not contain undefined invented words, that capitalization differences are a thin basis for legal arguments, and that requiring written permission is itself an OSD conflict.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Contends that the key qualifier in clause 4 is 'before obtaining written permission'—without permission, no endorsement is required—and offers to amend the clause for clarity.
timeline.point_zh: 辩称第4条关键在'before obtaining written permission'限定语，未获许可即无需推广，并愿为清晰度修订条款。
timeline.point: Contends that the key qualifier in clause 4 is 'before obtaining written permission'—without permission, no endorsement is required—and offers to amend the clause for clarity.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Accepts defining 'pronoic' within the license and amending clauses for clarity, and states intention to resubmit the revised version later.
timeline.point_zh: 接受在许可证内定义 pronoic、修订条款以提升清晰度，并表示将重新提交修订版。
timeline.point: Accepts defining 'pronoic' within the license and amending clauses for clarity, and states intention to resubmit the revised version later.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Points out the logical contradiction that clause 4's literal reading would require those without permission to use pronoic terms for promotion, while the actual intent seems to be the opposite; satirically questions the clause wording.
timeline.point_zh: 指出第4条字面逻辑要求未获许可者必须使用 pronoic 推广衍生作品，实际想要的恰是不使用的许可，讽刺条款措辞。
timeline.point: Points out the logical contradiction that clause 4's literal reading would require those without permission to use pronoic terms for promotion, while the actual intent seems to be the opposite; satirically questions the clause wording.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Questions how a court would distinguish someone who will never obtain permission from someone who has not yet decided, noting 'before obtaining permission' is equivalent to 'without permission', and suggests consulting a lawyer before submitting an unconventional license.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑法庭如何区分永不申请许可者与尚未决定者，指出'before obtaining permission'等同于'without permission'，建议提交非寻常许可证前咨询律师。
timeline.point: Questions how a court would distinguish someone who will never obtain permission from someone who has not yet decided, noting 'before obtaining permission' is equivalent to 'without permission', and suggests consulting a lawyer before submitting an unconventional license.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that clause 4 means using the company name or URL requires permission, pronoic as a term is bound to the company name without sacrificing its essence, and those adopting the license already agree with the pronoic spirit.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清第4条意为使用公司名/URL 须获许可，pronoic 一词绑定公司名而不损害其本质，采用该许可证者本身认同 pronoic 精神。
timeline.point: Clarifies that clause 4 means using the company name or URL requires permission, pronoic as a term is bound to the company name without sacrificing its essence, and those adopting the license already agree with the pronoic spirit.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Argues that 'before' means 'until you do', compares the distinction to Schrodinger's cat as unknowable until observed, and asserts that no breach occurs as long as contact is not made.
timeline.point_zh: 辩称'before'意为'直到你这样做'，并以薛定谔猫类比称无需区分申请者状态，未联系即不构成违约。
timeline.point: Argues that 'before' means 'until you do', compares the distinction to Schrodinger's cat as unknowable until observed, and asserts that no breach occurs as long as contact is not made.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Points out the clause's actual intent should be 'must not use the names without permission' rather than 'must be used', suggests rewriting accordingly might pass OSD, and stresses that license wording must be as precise as code.
timeline.point_zh: 指出条款实际意图应为'未经书面许可不得使用名称'而非'must be used'，若按此改写或可通过 OSD，并强调许可证措辞需如代码般严谨。
timeline.point: Points out the clause's actual intent should be 'must not use the names without permission' rather than 'must be used', suggests rewriting accordingly might pass OSD, and stresses that license wording must be as precise as code.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Thanks reviewers for the feedback and posts APOSSL version 1.2, amended to clarify the meaning of "pronoic" and the endorsement and naming clauses in response to the confusion raised.
timeline.point_zh: 感谢审阅者的反馈，并发布修订后的 APOSSL 1.2 版，针对引发的困惑澄清了 "pronoic" 的含义及背书与命名条款。
timeline.point: Thanks reviewers for the feedback and posts APOSSL version 1.2, amended to clarify the meaning of "pronoic" and the endorsement and naming clauses in response to the confusion raised.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Notes that v1.2 still does not comply with the OSD and provides correct pseudo-code logic with corresponding English wording: names must not be used without permission, and must be used when permission is granted.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 v1.2 仍不符 OSD，并给出正确伪代码逻辑及对应英文措辞示范：未获许可不得使用，获许可则必须使用。
timeline.point: Notes that v1.2 still does not comply with the OSD and provides correct pseudo-code logic with corresponding English wording: names must not be used without permission, and must be used when permission is granted.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Uses pseudo-code to restate the intended logic of clauses 4 and 5: using the pronoic term without permission is a breach of spirit rather than contract, while using the company name or Pronoic Ltd constitutes a breach of contract.
timeline.point_zh: 用伪代码重述第4、5条逻辑意图：未获许可时使用 pronoic 词仅属不符合精神而非违约，使用公司名/Pronoic Ltd 才构成违约。
timeline.point: Uses pseudo-code to restate the intended logic of clauses 4 and 5: using the pronoic term without permission is a breach of spirit rather than contract, while using the company name or Pronoic Ltd constitutes a breach of contract.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Agrees with the interpretation that clause 4 mandates the use of the pronoic name.
timeline.point_zh: 认同第4条强制使用 pronoic 名称的解读。
timeline.point: Agrees with the interpretation that clause 4 mandates the use of the pronoic name.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Revises clause 4 to 'should be used... before obtaining written permission' and presents the updated text.
timeline.point_zh: 将第4条修订为'should be used... before obtaining written permission'版本并展示新文本。
timeline.point: Revises clause 4 to 'should be used... before obtaining written permission' and presents the updated text.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Critiques the pseudo-code logic as self-contradictory, finds v1.2 still unclear, warns that unreachable clauses are taken seriously by courts, and questions whether the submitter is genuinely seeking OSI approval or just playing games.
timeline.point_zh: 批评伪代码逻辑自相矛盾、v1.2 仍未澄清问题，警告不可达条款会被法院不可预测地处置，并怀疑提交者只是戏弄列表而非真心寻求审批。
timeline.point: Critiques the pseudo-code logic as self-contradictory, finds v1.2 still unclear, warns that unreachable clauses are taken seriously by courts, and questions whether the submitter is genuinely seeking OSI approval or just playing games.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Satirically speculates that the APOSSL submitter may be playing a "guerrilla ontology" trick, doubting that the submission is a genuine bid for OSI approval.
timeline.point_zh: 讽刺性地猜测 APOSSL 提交者可能是在玩一种"游击本体论"式的把戏，怀疑其并非认真寻求 OSI 批准。
timeline.point: Satirically speculates that the APOSSL submitter may be playing a "guerrilla ontology" trick, doubting that the submission is a genuine bid for OSI approval.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Points out that clauses 4 and 5 of APOSSL address different uses of the term (promotional material vs. derivative work naming) and are not contradictory; believes the submitter has expressed intent via pseudocode that was then rewritten into prose.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 APOSSL 第4条与第5条针对术语的不同使用场景（推广材料 vs 衍生作品命名）并不矛盾，认为提交者已用伪代码表达意图并由此改写为正文。
timeline.point: Points out that clauses 4 and 5 of APOSSL address different uses of the term (promotional material vs. derivative work naming) and are not contradictory; believes the submitter has expressed intent via pseudocode that was then rewritten into prose.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Defends APOSSL v1.2's unconventional clauses, arguing the permission-to-use-term mechanism is workable and that off-beat goals are not grounds to deny OSI accreditation, refuting accusations of littering the license space.
timeline.point_zh: 为 APOSSL v1.2 的非传统条款辩护，认为使用术语须经许可的机制可行，且古怪的目标不构成拒绝 OSI 认可的理由，并反驳了污染许可证领域的指责。
timeline.point: Defends APOSSL v1.2's unconventional clauses, arguing the permission-to-use-term mechanism is workable and that off-beat goals are not grounds to deny OSI accreditation, refuting accusations of littering the license space.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Argues that clause 4 contradicts the submitter's stated refusal to grant permission, constituting an offer in bad faith; recommends the board reject it as a self-referential paradox and suggests using the Apache license instead.
timeline.point_zh: 指出第4条与提交者"永不授权"的说法自相矛盾、构成恶意要约，建议董事会以"自指悖论"为由坚决拒绝该许可证并改用 Apache 许可证。
timeline.point: Argues that clause 4 contradicts the submitter's stated refusal to grant permission, constituting an offer in bad faith; recommends the board reject it as a self-referential paradox and suggests using the Apache license instead.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Satirically parodies the APOSSL terms regarding pronoic terminology usage and permission requests in the form of haiku.
timeline.point_zh: 以讽刺性俳句嘲弄 APOSSL 关于 pronoic 术语使用与授权请求的条款。
timeline.point: Satirically parodies the APOSSL terms regarding pronoic terminology usage and permission requests in the form of haiku.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that permission is not permanently denied but rather that the right to refuse is reserved; maintains the license is unusual but not paradoxical, and questions whether the board is acting as a review body rather than an accreditation one.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清并非永不授权而是保留拒绝权，认为许可证本身并不悖论只是不寻常，并质疑对方以审查而非认证的标准对待该许可证。
timeline.point: Clarifies that permission is not permanently denied but rather that the right to refuse is reserved; maintains the license is unusual but not paradoxical, and questions whether the board is acting as a review body rather than an accreditation one.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Contends that APOSSL without its special clauses is functionally equivalent to the BSD license, accuses the submitter of failing to explain existing license deficiencies, and regards the submission as pointless license proliferation.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 APOSSL 去掉特殊条款后与 BSD 功能等同，指责提交者未说明现有许可证的不足、实为在 OSSL 领域制造冗余。
timeline.point: Contends that APOSSL without its special clauses is functionally equivalent to the BSD license, accuses the submitter of failing to explain existing license deficiencies, and regards the submission as pointless license proliferation.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: States that the discussion board is weary of yet another new license and considers the submitter's attitude to be toying with the group.
timeline.point_zh: 表示讨论板对又冒出一个新许可证普遍感到厌烦，认为提交者的态度是在戏弄大家。
timeline.point: States that the discussion board is weary of yet another new license and considers the submitter's attitude to be toying with the group.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Uses a self-referential sentence structure to imply that the APOSSL approval request will be rejected.
timeline.point_zh: 以自指句式暗示 APOSSL 的批准请求将被拒绝。
timeline.point: Uses a self-referential sentence structure to imply that the APOSSL approval request will be rejected.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Continues using self-referential sentences to suggest the license will be rejected or set aside, and asks the submitter to move on.
timeline.point_zh: 继续用自指句式暗示该许可证会被拒绝或搁置，并要求提交者停止纠缠。
timeline.point: Continues using self-referential sentences to suggest the license will be rejected or set aside, and asks the submitter to move on.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Agrees with the interpretation that clause 4 mandates use of the pronoic term, finds clause 5 unclear in its behavioral requirements, and suggests the license needs clearer drafting.
timeline.point_zh: 认同第4条强制要求使用 pronoic 术语的解读，指出第5条含义不明，认为该许可证需要写得更清楚。
timeline.point: Agrees with the interpretation that clause 4 mandates use of the pronoic term, finds clause 5 unclear in its behavioral requirements, and suggests the license needs clearer drafting.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: In an off-topic quine discussion, rebuts that the opponent's sentence structure does not constitute a valid quine and questions their authoritative tone.
timeline.point_zh: 在跑题的 quine 讨论中反驳对方的句式不构成有效 quine，并质疑其以权威口吻发言。
timeline.point: In an off-topic quine discussion, rebuts that the opponent's sentence structure does not constitute a valid quine and questions their authoritative tone.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Uses self-referential sentences to express the consensus of many commenters: the license would be rejected if approval is sought, but is harmless if no approval is requested.
timeline.point_zh: 用自指句式表达多数评论者认为该许可证在申请批准时会被拒绝、只要不申请批准就无碍。
timeline.point: Uses self-referential sentences to express the consensus of many commenters: the license would be rejected if approval is sought, but is harmless if no approval is requested.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Uses a self-referential sentence to humorously suggest that even the discussion of this license is more relevant to the mailing list's purpose than the license itself.
timeline.point_zh: 以自指句式调侃，暗示关于该许可证的讨论本身都比该许可证更切合邮件列表宗旨。
timeline.point: Uses a self-referential sentence to humorously suggest that even the discussion of this license is more relevant to the mailing list's purpose than the license itself.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Continues the off-topic quine debate, pointing out that the opponent's sentences lack coherent semantics and do not form a true quine.
timeline.point_zh: 继续在跑题的 quine 讨论中指出对方的句式语义不成立、不构成真正的 quine。
timeline.point: Continues the off-topic quine debate, pointing out that the opponent's sentences lack coherent semantics and do not form a true quine.

timeline.subject: request for approval of APOSSL
timeline.snippet: Humbly wraps up the quine side discussion, noting for future readers that serious licenses receive serious discussion on this list.
timeline.point_zh: 自谦并收尾 quine 讨论，留言提示后人：严肃的许可证在此列表会得到严肃讨论。
timeline.point: Humbly wraps up the quine side discussion, noting for future readers that serious licenses receive serious discussion on this list.

submissions.rejection_reason: Never approved. The license's anti-piracy focus imposed restrictions inconsistent with the OSD.

submissions.name: qmail License

curated_rwp.rejection_reason: Never approved. qmail's license (by Daniel Bernstein) had distribution restrictions that violated OSD.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Argues qmail's license terms pass OSD clause 4 and the other OSD clauses, since the patch-file allowance is superfluous under copyright law; urges OSI to either approve qmail as OSD-conformant or clarify clause 4, a flaw that effectively prevents forking.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 qmail 许可证条款符合 OSD 第 4 条及其他条款——补丁文件要求在版权法下是多余的;敦促 OSI 要么批准 qmail 符合 OSD,要么澄清他认为妨碍分叉的第 4 条缺陷。
timeline.point: Argues qmail's license terms pass OSD clause 4 and the other OSD clauses, since the patch-file allowance is superfluous under copyright law; urges OSI to either approve qmail as OSD-conformant or clarify clause 4, a flaw that effectively prevents forking.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Acknowledges possible technical workarounds but ultimately rejects qmail's restrictive distribution terms.
timeline.point_zh: 承认可以用工具绕开部分限制，但最终仍否定 qmail 的发行限制。
timeline.point: Acknowledges possible technical workarounds but ultimately rejects qmail's restrictive distribution terms.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Says qmail may allow forking in theory but still raises doubts about whether it satisfies OSD clause 4.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 qmail 在理论上允许分叉，但仍对其是否满足 OSD 第 4 条表示怀疑。
timeline.point: Says qmail may allow forking in theory but still raises doubts about whether it satisfies OSD clause 4.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Clarifies that qmail permits some older binary distributions and that the page's date limits are not the whole story.
timeline.point_zh: 说明 qmail 允许分发某些旧版二进制，页面上的日期限制并不是全部含义。
timeline.point: Clarifies that qmail permits some older binary distributions and that the page's date limits are not the whole story.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Argues that patch-based workflows still permit forking and that the OSD should focus on practical freedom, including binaries.
timeline.point_zh: 主张补丁式流程仍然可以分叉，OSD 应关注实际自由，包括二进制分发。
timeline.point: Argues that patch-based workflows still permit forking and that the OSD should focus on practical freedom, including binaries.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Defends sharing patches but says the OSD still does not clearly require binary distribution rights.
timeline.point_zh: 为补丁分享辩护，但认为 OSD 仍未清楚要求必须允许二进制分发。
timeline.point: Defends sharing patches but says the OSD still does not clearly require binary distribution rights.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Says qmail-style workarounds are awkward and does not treat privileged participation as a problem in itself.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 qmail 式绕行会带来很多别扭边角问题，但并不把特权参与本身视为问题。
timeline.point: Says qmail-style workarounds are awkward and does not treat privileged participation as a problem in itself.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Says qmail-style patch sharing is not enough for the spirit of open source because binaries matter too.
timeline.point_zh: 认为仅靠补丁分享不足以体现开源精神，因为二进制分发同样重要。
timeline.point: Says qmail-style patch sharing is not enough for the spirit of open source because binaries matter too.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Defends qmail's restrictions as compatible with open source and asks for real-world examples of failure.
timeline.point_zh: 为 qmail 的限制辩护，认为它仍可算开源，并要求举出失败的现实例子。
timeline.point: Defends qmail's restrictions as compatible with open source and asks for real-world examples of failure.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Rejects the claim that qmail's conditions are acceptable because they are still not an explicit permission to distribute modified builds.
timeline.point_zh: 否认 qmail 条件可接受，认为它并未明确允许分发由修改源代码构建的软件。
timeline.point: Rejects the claim that qmail's conditions are acceptable because they are still not an explicit permission to distribute modified builds.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Argues that qmail should count because it allows binaries under conditions, even if source releases are constrained.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 qmail 应算合格，因为它在一定条件下允许二进制分发，尽管源码发布受限。
timeline.point: Argues that qmail should count because it allows binaries under conditions, even if source releases are constrained.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Concludes that the qmail page does not satisfy OSD clause 4 because it does not truly allow binaries from modified source.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 qmail 页面并不满足 OSD 第 4 条，因为它并未真正允许由修改源码生成的二进制分发。
timeline.point: Concludes that the qmail page does not satisfy OSD clause 4 because it does not truly allow binaries from modified source.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Says qmail's binary restrictions violate OSD clause 4 if the words are read in their ordinary sense.
timeline.point_zh: 认为如果按通常含义理解，qmail 的二进制限制违反了 OSD 第 4 条。
timeline.point: Says qmail's binary restrictions violate OSD clause 4 if the words are read in their ordinary sense.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Argues that conditional permission can be so restrictive that it does not count as real permission.
timeline.point_zh: 主张附条件的许可可能过于苛刻，因此不算真正的许可。
timeline.point: Argues that conditional permission can be so restrictive that it does not count as real permission.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Calls the patch-based reading semantic evasion: the OSD requires licenses to explicitly allow distribution, not to disallow it conditionally; notes no one, including DJB, actually claims qmail is open source, and Darren's conflicting statements make the IPF license's intent unreliable.
timeline.point_zh: 斥这种补丁解读为语义闪避:OSD 要求许可证明确允许分发,而非附条件地不允许;指出包括 DJB 在内无人真称 qmail 是开源,IPF 许可证的意图陈述也互相矛盾。
timeline.point: Calls the patch-based reading semantic evasion: the OSD requires licenses to explicitly allow distribution, not to disallow it conditionally; notes no one, including DJB, actually claims qmail is open source, and Darren's conflicting statements make the IPF license's intent unreliable.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Uses a bug-fix example to argue that qmail still allows modified binaries to be redistributed under its conditions.
timeline.point_zh: 用修复 bug 的例子说明 qmail 仍允许在其条件下重新分发修改后的二进制。
timeline.point: Uses a bug-fix example to argue that qmail still allows modified binaries to be redistributed under its conditions.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Notes that all licenses impose conditions, so qmail's use of conditions is not unusual by itself.
timeline.point_zh: 指出所有许可证都会附带条件，因此 qmail 使用条件并不罕见。
timeline.point: Notes that all licenses impose conditions, so qmail's use of conditions is not unusual by itself.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Rebuts the misreading charge by noting the GPL itself conditions redistribution; maintains that pristine-source-plus-patches licenses serve distributors but deny the right to fork, and urges an OSD clarification so its letter matches its spirit.
timeline.point_zh: 以 GPL 本身也附带再分发条件来反驳误读指控;坚持“原始源码加补丁”式许可只利分发商而剥夺分叉权,并呼吁澄清 OSD 使条文字面契合其精神。
timeline.point: Rebuts the misreading charge by noting the GPL itself conditions redistribution; maintains that pristine-source-plus-patches licenses serve distributors but deny the right to fork, and urges an OSD clarification so its letter matches its spirit.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Frames open source as a positive permission to share rather than a control mechanism.
timeline.point_zh: 把开源定义为允许分享的正向许可，而不是控制机制。
timeline.point: Frames open source as a positive permission to share rather than a control mechanism.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Counters that fixing a core-dumping qmail build does change behavior, so the modified version is not equivalent to the original.
timeline.point_zh: 反驳说，修复会崩溃的 qmail 构建会改变行为，因此修改版并不等同于原版。
timeline.point: Counters that fixing a core-dumping qmail build does change behavior, so the modified version is not equivalent to the original.

timeline.subject: license submission: qmail
timeline.snippet: Argues that OSD clause 3 means a derived qmail build may not be redistributed on the original terms, while welcoming edge-case discussion.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 OSD 第 3 条意味着 qmail 的衍生构建不能按原条款再分发，同时欢迎讨论边界情况。
timeline.point: Argues that OSD clause 3 means a derived qmail build may not be redistributed on the original terms, while welcoming edge-case discussion.

submissions.rejection_reason: Never approved. qmail's license (by Daniel Bernstein) had distribution restrictions that violated OSD.

transparent attribution of AI involvement at the file level.

timeline.point: Agrees with the view that AI-generated code will become uncopyrightable, sharing a related article link, but adds the caveat that ideally the AI should be Open Source AI as defined, and it is too early to tell whether machines can self-maintain generated code.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Notes copyrightability of computer-generated works varies by jurisdiction (e.g. UK s9(3) CDPA 1988 and database right), and argues the community should be extremely wary of setting licensing norms around AI-generated code while the underlying IP rights are unclear.
timeline.point_zh: 指出计算机生成作品的可版权性因辖区而异（如英国CDPA 1988 s9(3)、数据库权），并主张在底层IP权利不明时应对为AI生成代码设立许可规范保持高度警惕。
timeline.point: Notes copyrightability of computer-generated works varies by jurisdiction (e.g. UK s9(3) CDPA 1988 and database right), and argues the community should be extremely wary of setting licensing norms around AI-generated code while the underlying IP rights are unclear.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Argues copyright in AI-generated code attaches to the human creative contribution across most jurisdictions, so licensing still works; is cautious about AI-MIT/AIAL because a license should not predetermine the legal status of AI-generated portions or add special notice obligations.
timeline.point_zh: 认为多数法域下 AI 生成代码的版权归于人类创造性贡献,许可机制仍然有效;对 AI-MIT/AIAL 持谨慎态度,因许可证不应预设 AI 生成部分的法律地位并附加特别声明义务。
timeline.point: Argues copyright in AI-generated code attaches to the human creative contribution across most jurisdictions, so licensing still works; is cautious about AI-MIT/AIAL because a license should not predetermine the legal status of AI-generated portions or add special notice obligations.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] [SUBMISSION] AI-MIT License 1.0 — permissive license for AI-generated code
timeline.snippet: Highlights two major risks: that informal community norms can be codified into law by courts, and that the community generally overestimates the power of licenses and underestimates the limits of copyright, leading to conflicts with companies and disappointment in court.
timeline.point_zh: 强调两大风险：社区非正式规范会被法院固化为法律，以及社区普遍高估许可证与版权的效力、低估其边界，导致与公司冲突并在法庭上失望。

2、Rationale for Submission

While permissive licenses like MIT and Apache 2.0 are excellent and widely used, we believe the QmDeve License 1.0 addresses a specific combination of needs that is not fully met by existing options:

· Simplicity and Clarity: It retains the straightforward language and minimal restrictions of the MIT license.
· Explicit Patent Protection: Unlike the MIT license, it includes an explicit, modern patent grant and termination clause, similar to Apache 2.0, which provides crucial legal safety for users and contributors in today's software landscape.
· Trademark Protection: It includes a no-endorsement clause (like BSD-3-Clause and Apache 2.0) to protect the "QmDeve" organization name and identity from being used to endorse derived products without permission.
· Contributor Clarity: It explicitly states that contributions are licensed under the same terms, clarifying the inbound-outbound contribution process for projects.

We believe this combination—a truly permissive core, coupled with explicit patent and trademark protections—creates a balanced and secure license for modern open-source projects.

3、Check against the Open Source Definition (OSD)

We affirm that the QmDeve License 1.0 conforms to all ten criteria of the Open Source Definition:

1. Free Redistribution: Yes. Permits redistribution and sale.
2. Source Code: Yes. Source code can be freely distributed.
3. Derived Works: Yes. Allows creation and distribution of modifications and derived works.
4. Integrity of The Author's Source Code: Yes. Condition 1 preserves copyright notices.
5. No Discrimination Against Persons or Groups: Yes.
6. No Discrimination Against Fields of Endeavor: Yes.
7. Distribution of License: Yes. The license applies automatically to all redistributors.
8. License Must Not Be Specific to a Product: Yes. The license is not tied to a specific product.
9. License Must Not Restrict Other Software: Yes. It does not place restrictions on other software distributed alongside it.
10. License Must Be Technology-Neutral: Yes. The license is not specific to any technology or interface.


4、Proliferation and Redundancy Analysis

We have analyzed this license against the MIT and Apache 2.0 licenses.

· vs. MIT: The QmDeve License 1.0 provides significant additional protections (patent and trademark) that the MIT license lacks, addressing a modern legal concern.
· vs. Apache 2.0: While Apache 2.0 is a comprehensive license, it is longer and more complex. The QmDeve License 1.0 aims for a middle ground—providing similar core protections (patent, trademark) but in a potentially more accessible format. We believe this fills a niche for projects that want stronger legal safeguards than MIT but prefer a different structure than Apache 2.0.

This license is currently planned for use by projects under the "QmDeve" organization on GitHub. We are seeking OSI approval to ensure its legitimacy and foster wider community adoption.

*Released under the Open Innovation License*

Copyright © // Insert information of license holder

*Version 1, 10th November 2020*

*Copyright © 2020 Stark Drones Corporation*
*Copyright © 2020 Andrew Magdy Kamal*

This project is licensed under the *Open Innovation License*. This means
any code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation containing this
license within it can be copied, modified, redistributed, published, or
even used for commercial purposes within the context of this license.
Any code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation containing this
license is understood to be fully "AS IS", no claims are made in regards to
safety, security, warranty, usability, or other form of merchantability and
market-readiness. In no events are copyright holders, authors, or
publishers are to be held liable for any claims, damage or results from
usage of what have been licensed under this license.

The context of this license includes: Keeping this original license text
verbatim and permissive notice, as well as the copyright notice included in
any redistribution of said project. Project is defined as what is using
this license. For purposes of context, the copyright notice above version
and year is meant to be modified for whomsoever publishes or releases "any
code, file, diagrams, data format, or other innovation", so that they can
include their information. After modifying, the comment saying "// Insert
information of license holder" which starts with // can be removed. This
current paragraph however, will remain in-tact.

Anybody who releases software under the "Open Innovation License" agrees to
at goodwill, build or release technology for the betterment of humanity not
meant with the intention to harm a human being. They agree to a prima facie
moral duty through consequential deontology to understand that technology
should be within the concept of moral good or outcomes that are morally
right and/or ethical. They agree at goodwill to promote the advancement of
humanity and civilization as a whole. They agree to a sense of
adventurement, edification, and the expansion of the human mind.

Said agreement which is within the last paragraph prior to this sentence is
meant to be taken as a general consensus, but not legally enforceable.
Again for context, the last paragraph which starts with "Anybody" and ends
with "human mind" minus quotations, is outside of the boundaries of being
legally enforceable and within the duties of oneselve's actions. The rest
of the license which includes the copyright notice and its context is
within a legally enforceable context. For secondary context, the rest of
the license refers to anything outside of that said paragraph.

____

*Rationale:*

I wanted to release this license for a variety of different reasons.
Infact, I made many posts in regards to why this license is unique and
valuable, and found many developers willing to adapt this license through
small innovation challenges. The license was made on the basis of promoting
a mission statement on ethical technology within the license as well as not
being specific to only software i.e. files, diagrams, data format or any
other innovation.

We also wanted to make sure that the license is adaptable. Many open source
licenses require you to put tons of header files for compliance. We wanted
to make a license that just requires you to contain the license file in
your directory. While many other open source licenses also do that or
follow in similar footsteps, we weren't able to find one that met all these
unique qualities.

Currently, a big inspiration for this license was the idea of promoting
free and open software as well as a mission statement on ethical
technologies. We found that many of the big tech companies that are hailed
as heroes of open source or doing open source initiatives, built
technologies that are harmful to human activity. A technically non-legally
enforceable mission statement within an enforceable open source license was
the way to go. We also made sure to go out of our way to promote the ideals
of open source and free and redistributive software.

*Distinguish:*

I looked at a variety of different open source licenses. The standard being
MIT, then BSD+Patent, ZLib, CDDL, CPAL, CPL, CAL, BSL, and the AFL license.
I feel like MIT, ZLIB, and the Boost licenses focus on redistribution and
code. Those are the standards. The open patent licenses and other licenses
focus on derived original work. However, none of them tried going to the
same extent I wanted in terms of being specific in regards to data formats
or general consensus and mission. I believe this is an important thing to
take into account.

*Legal review:*

Currently I have submitted this to SPDX as well for review through their
GitHub/Website. However, the review time to get approval and receive SPDX
identifiers can be many months. I submitted in November and decided to
submit to OSI while I wait. As for reviewing the context of language myself
and actual legal review, I have thought out reviews through my own legal
council and self judgement as a researcher familiar with these types of
languages.

*Proliferation category:*

I don't necessarily need to be in a Proliferation category as of now, as
many of the licenses on your site are not in a category. However, I would
eventually want to get into the *Licenses that are popular and widely used
or with strong communities *category.
