timeline.point: Questions the definition of "extended version" versus "derivative work" and notes that "any portion" is too broad.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Project Public License (OPPL)

timeline.subject: discuss: EPD CORE OPEN SOURCE LICENSE - Version 0.1

timeline.point: Submits the EPD Core Open Source License 0.1 for OSI approval, a deliberately simplified Motosoto-derived license, and offers to retract it if an existing approved license covers the same bases.
timeline.point_zh: 提交 EPD Core Open Source License 0.1 供 OSI 审批，这是一个刻意简化的、源自 Motosoto 的许可证；若现有已批准许可证能覆盖同样内容，愿意撤回。

timeline.subject: discuss: EPD CORE OPEN SOURCE LICENSE - Version 0.1
timeline.snippet: On Thursday 13 February 2003 09:06 pm, Bill Moran wrote: > [ Please discuss this license. -russ ] > > I have attached a license that we are proposing to be OSI compliant. > The li
timeline.point: Suggests crafting the license as a template to allow reuse without re-approval, argues against requiring users to agree to the license for usage, and warns about onerous restrictions and warranties.
timeline.point_zh: 建议将许可证制成模板以便复用而无需重新批准，反对要求用户同意许可证才能使用，并提醒注意繁重限制与担保。

timeline.subject: discuss: EPD CORE OPEN SOURCE LICENSE - Version 0.1

timeline.point: Accepts several review suggestions—reworking clause 1 along QPL lines and posting a v0.2—while defending the requirement that the author warrant ownership of the code as not violating the open source definition.
timeline.point_zh: 接受多项评审意见，将参照 QPL 修改第 1 条并发布 v0.2，同时坚持要求作者保证代码所有权的要求并不违反开源定义。

timeline.subject: discuss: EPD CORE OPEN SOURCE LICENSE - Version 0.1

timeline.point: Argues all contributors should warrant their IP in their contributions, and suggests stripping the license down to a QPL-based paragraph 1 plus the module clause so it will be obviously an open-source license.
timeline.point_zh: 主张所有贡献者都应为自己的知识产权作担保，并建议将许可证精简为基于 Q Public License 的第 1 条加模块条款，使其显然符合开源定义。

timeline.subject: discuss: EPD CORE OPEN SOURCE LICENSE - Version 0.1

timeline.point: Asks for advice on whether to create a new derivative license or simply use the QPL with a clarifying clause, questioning if a new license is necessary.
timeline.point_zh: 就创建新衍生许可证还是直接使用 QPL 加澄清条款征求意见，质疑是否有必要制定新许可证。

timeline.subject: discuss: EPD CORE OPEN SOURCE LICENSE - Version 0.1
timeline.snippet: Bill Moran scripsit: > How, exactly, should we approach this? Create a new license that contains > the above verbage, which would be a derivative of the QPL, or is that > overkill
timeline.point: States that using the QPL with a clarifying paragraph sounds acceptable, but advises against creating new licenses to reduce community analysis burden.

timeline.subject: discuss: EPD CORE OPEN SOURCE LICENSE - Version 0.1

timeline.point: Posts version 0.2 of the EPD Core Open Source License, incorporating many suggestions from the list, noting continued dissatisfaction with the QPL and inviting further discussion.

timeline.point: Argues the license contains unnecessary provisions and suggests paragraph 3 needs work to ensure compliance with OSD #2 regarding source code availability.

timeline.point: Submits the OPEN TOM PUBLIC LICENSE (OTPL) version 1.2 for discussion, describing it as a permissive license with source distribution and patent grant requirements.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] [NEW LICENSE] OTPL (OPEN TOM PUBLIC LICENSE) v1.0

submissions.name: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL)
aliases: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
timeline.snippet: I'd like to announce two more prospective licenses, brought to you by OpenVendor.org (which is currently David Ryan and me, until we put together something more formal). These are
timeline.point: Announces the OVPL and OVLPL, CDDL-based reciprocal licenses with patent-defence clauses designed to let commercial developers open existing code while keeping a commercial version, and asks for comment rather than formal approval.
timeline.point_zh: 发布基于 CDDL 的 OVPL 与 OVLPL——含专利防御条款的互惠许可证，供商业代码开源之用——并征求意见而非申请正式批准。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
timeline.snippet: While not specifically aimed at openvendor.org, the question can be asked, over similar licenses, why should contributors give specific privileges to the initial developers? Shoul
timeline.point: Questions why contributors should give specific privileges to initial developers instead of treating all parties equally, suggesting separate commercial licensing negotiations instead.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑为何贡献者应给予初始开发者特定特权而非各方平等对待，建议改为另行协商商业许可。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
timeline.snippet: --On 10 April 2005 05:31 -0700 Andy Tai <lichengtai at yahoo.com> wrote: > While not specifically aimed at openvendor.org, the > question can be asked, over similar licenses, why
timeline.point: Defends the additional license grant to the Initial Developer: for preexisting closed-source code, the commercial tree is the quid-pro-quo for open-sourcing, and the grant also eases relicensing and dual licensing for the community.
timeline.point_zh: 为初始开发者的额外许可授权辩护：既有闭源代码需以商业分支作为开源的交换条件，该条款也便于社区后续改许可与双许可。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
timeline.snippet: I haven't looked at this for OSD compliance, but am making a comment on the covenant between you and the outside developers. Is your intention to vend an _enhanced_ version of the
timeline.point: Suggests balancing the relationship between the initial developer and contributors by requiring the open source version to be maintained alongside any proprietary version to avoid second-class citizen status.
timeline.point_zh: 建议要求开源版本与任何专有版本并行维护，以平衡初始开发者与贡献者关系，避免二等公民地位。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
timeline.snippet: Technically, I think you could use the existing CDDL or even another license and make the right to relicense a separate document which must be entered into in order for a modifica
timeline.point: Suggests using a separate document for the right to relicense rather than embedding it in the license itself, similar to Sun's copyright assignment model.
timeline.point_zh: 建议将重新授权权利放在单独文件中而非嵌入许可证本身，类似于 Sun 的版权转让模式。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
timeline.snippet: Bruce, --On 10 April 2005 10:10 -0700 Bruce Perens <bruce at perens.com> wrote: > I haven't looked at this for OSD compliance, but am making a comment on > the covenant between yo
timeline.point: Clarifies that outside contributions must by definition remain in the open-source version: the ID receives the additional license only provided those versions stay available under the license per Section 4.1.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清外部贡献按定义必须保留在开源版本中：初始开发者仅以相关版本依本许可证持续可用为条件（Section 4.1）获得额外许可。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
timeline.snippet: --On 10 April 2005 10:14 -0700 Bruce Perens <bruce at perens.com> wrote: > Technically, I think you could use the existing CDDL or even another > license and make the right to rel
timeline.point: Explains that the OVPL requires contributors to license modifications to the Initial Developer, contrasting this with a separate copyright assignment approach.
timeline.point_zh: 说明 OVPL 要求贡献者将修改授权给 Initial Developer，并将其与单独的版权转让方式作对比。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
timeline.snippet: Bruce, --On 10 April 2005 18:54 +0100 Alex Bligh <alex at alex.org.uk> wrote: > That's already there isn't it - the bit of 4.1 I mentioned? OK it may have been there, but it wasn'
timeline.point: Posts a redrafted Section 3.3 clarifying that anything used in a commercial version must also remain available in an open-source version, and welcomes further drafting suggestions.
timeline.point_zh: 发布重写的 Section 3.3，澄清商业版本中使用的任何修改也必须持续以开源版本提供，并欢迎进一步的措辞修改建议。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
timeline.snippet: Under what circumstances are developers required to provide code back to the ID? Am I correct in assuming that code needs to be provided/licensed back to the ID if one chooses to
timeline.point: Questions whether licensing modifications back to the Initial Developer satisfies OSD #1 (Free Redistribution) and #5 (No Discrimination Against Persons or Groups), and doubts the license qualifies as open source despite its vendor benefits.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑向初始开发者回馈许可的规定是否满足 OSD 第 1 条（Free Redistribution）与第 5 条，怀疑该许可证能否算作开源。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
timeline.snippet: Kevin Bedell wrote: >If the license requires me to provide a license to the ID of my >modifications in order for me to redistribute code under the license, I'd >question whether o
timeline.point: Argues that an additional rights grant to the original developer is not discriminatory under OSD #5 and allows free redistribution, passing the fields-of-endeavor test.

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL

timeline.point_zh: 为 OVPL 赋予 Initial Developer 的额外权利辩护,称其符合 QPL 先例,否认构成歧视,并主张该许可证符合 OSD,尽管不如 GPL 或 BSD 纯粹。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL

timeline.point: Compares the license to the OSI-approved SISSL, which also has technical redistribution restrictions, questioning if similar restrictions are truly OSD violations.
timeline.point_zh: 将该许可证与OSI批准的SISSL比较，后者同样有技术再分发限制，质疑类似限制是否真属违反OSD。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL
timeline.snippet: Bruce, Thanks for the clarifications. My concerns are met. -kevin -- Kevin Bedell Black Duck Software 100 Beaver St Waltham, MA 02453 http://www.blackducksoftware.com (p) 781-891-
timeline.point: States that previous concerns about the license have been met by the clarifications provided.
timeline.point_zh: 表示此前对该许可证的担忧已通过所提供的澄清得到解决。

timeline.subject: Two new licenses - OVPL & OVLPL

timeline.point: Formally submits the OVPL and OVLPL (Open Vendor Public License and Open Vendor Lesser Public License) for OSI approval, describing them as CDDL-based modern reciprocal licenses with patent defence clauses that grant the Initial Developer additional rights.
timeline.point_zh: 正式提交 OVPL 与 OVLPL 供 OSI 审批,称其为基于 CDDL 的现代互惠许可证,含专利防御条款,并赋予 Initial Developer 额外权利。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: Alex Bligh wrote: > Matthew, > > --On 03 June 2005 22:05 +0000 Matthew Seth Flaschen > <superm40 at comcast.net> wrote: > >> The license would then imply that you couldn't distrib
timeline.point: Expresses willingness to cooperate but indicates a solution is needed.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)

timeline.point: Requests an update on the license submission status following the monthly review deadline.
timeline.point_zh: 请求在月度评审截止后更新许可证提交状态。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)

timeline.point_zh: 请求OSI更新许可证提交状态，询问其已被接受、被拒绝还是尚未评审。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: There has been very little response from the community regarding the request for approval of these two licenses. As one of the people who worked hard to create these licenses I wo

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: David Ryan wrote: > If you believe there is any value to having these licenses approved by > the OSI, can you *please* reply to the list casting your vote to have > them approved.
timeline.point: Votes -1, arguing that new licenses are unnecessary because the stated goal can be achieved using existing licenses and contributor agreements.
timeline.point_zh: 投票-1，认为新许可证不必要，因为所述目标可通过现有许可证和贡献者协议实现。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: Andrew, > Well, you asked for it: I'm going to vote -1 for the following reason. I > think the originators of OVPL and OVLPL have done an admirably > conscientious job of drafting
timeline.point: Argues the OVPL's built-in license-back is superior to separate contribution agreements—avoiding unsigned consents, unreviewed terms, and IPR disputes—and urges reversal of the objection, claiming the license meets the OSD and is not a duplicate.
timeline.point_zh: 主张 OVPL 内置的 license-back 优于单独的贡献者协议,可避免未签署同意、条款不受审查及知识产权纠纷,并敦促撤回反对意见,称该许可证符合 OSD 且非重复。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: I've been looking around for how this was solved before. I remember reading a license which has a specific carve-out where the licensed product is a compiler, to ensure that objec
timeline.point: Asks for help identifying an OSI-approved license that contains a carve-out exempting a compiler's output from the license terms.

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: Perhaps you are thinking about the exception to the Bison product: http://www.gnu.org/software/bison/manual/html_mono/bison.html#Conditions Conditions for Using Bison As of Bison
timeline.point: Points to the GNU Bison 'special exception' as prior art: since Bison 1.24, the yyparse output may be used in nonfree programs, limiting GPL coverage of compiler output.
timeline.point_zh: 援引 GNU Bison 的"特别例外"作为先例:自 Bison 1.24 起,yyparse 输出可用于非自由程序,限制了 GPL 对编译器输出的覆盖。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: --On 30 June 2005 08:36 -0400 peter.moldave at gesmer.com wrote: > Perhaps you are thinking about the exception to the Bison product: > > http://www.gnu.org/software/bison/manual/
timeline.point: Notes that while the Bison license was not the specific one recalled, it addresses the exact same issue regarding output generated by a tool.
timeline.point_zh: 指出虽然回忆起的并非Bison许可证，但它解决的正是工具生成输出方面的同一问题。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: Alex Bligh writes: > I've been looking around for how this was solved before. > > I remember reading a license which has a specific carve-out where the > licensed product is a com
timeline.point: Notes the FSF already uses GPL/LGPL add-on exceptions in GNU components such as libstdc++, libgcc, glibc, and libgcj, with language tailored to each library's expected uses.
timeline.point_zh: 指出 FSF 已在 libstdc++、libgcc、glibc、libgcj 等 GNU 组件中使用 GPL/LGPL 附加例外,且措辞因各库预期用途而异。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: --On 30 June 2005 14:00 +0100 Alex Bligh <alex at alex.org.uk> wrote: >> Perhaps you are thinking about the exception to the Bison product: >> >> http://www.gnu.org/software/bison
timeline.point: Identifies a clause in the GPL that states output is covered only if it constitutes a work based on the program, independent of the act of running it.
timeline.point_zh: 指出GPL中一项条款：输出仅在其构成基于该程序的作品时才受约束，与运行行为无关。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: The exception in Bison is necessary because of this clause. This clause does not (in my opinion) give you enough comfort to say a program that inserts itself in the source code. T
timeline.point: Argues the GPL clause covering copied text in output means parser/compiler output can be subject to the GPL at some level — which is why the Bison exception was necessary and why that clause alone offers no comfort.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 GPL 中复制进输出的文本仍受原许可证约束的条款，意味着输出在一定程度上会受 GPL 约束，Bison 正因此才需要例外。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: --On 30 June 2005 09:10 -0400 mdpoole <mdpoole at troilus.org> wrote: > As Peter Muldave showed, add-ons to the GPL and LGPL are used by the > FSF in several components of the GNU
timeline.point: Distinguishes the output-derived-work issue from library linking, notes initial developers can address output concerns via an additional-grant exception, and asks whether a general exception should be explicit in the license, leaning toward leaving it to the ID.
timeline.point_zh: 区分输出衍生作品问题与库链接问题；认为初始开发者可通过附加授权例外解决输出担忧，并询问是否应将该例外明确写入许可证。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: --On 30 June 2005 09:31 -0400 peter.moldave at gesmer.com wrote: > The part of the second paragraph that says "the copied text in the output > is covered by the same license that
timeline.point: Suggests that handling output exceptions via an additional grant might be clearer than embedding the terms in the license itself.
timeline.point_zh: 建议通过额外授权处理输出例外，可能比将条款嵌入许可证本身更清晰。

timeline.subject: For Approval: Open Vendor Public License (OVPL) and Open Vendor Lesser Public License (OVLPL)
timeline.snippet: Alex Bligh wrote: > You are quite correct that IF every contributor signed a contribution > agreement, then the effect would not doubt be the same (for the initial > developer) as
timeline.point: Finds a coercive whiff in OVPL/OVLPL's mandatory license-back to the initial developer, calling coercion inappropriate in an open source license, and remains at -1.

the GPLicense since security aspects are not covered by the GPL:

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License
timeline.snippet: I recently decided I wanted to release a project of mine as open source, so I set out to find a license that suited me. In the grand tradition of computer programmers everywhere,
timeline.point: Submits a self-written license for review, noting it currently lacks a provision for distributing modified binaries.
timeline.point_zh: 提交一份自写许可证供审查，指出其目前缺少分发修改后二进制文件的条款。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License
timeline.snippet: Bruce Perens wrote: > > From: Alex Nicolaou <anicolao at cgl.uwaterloo.ca> > > You may not distribute versions of the software with your patch applied, > > although you may includ
timeline.point: Clarifies that the modification return requirement is an "OR" condition, arguing it does not burden distributors like Debian.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清修改回报要求是“OR”（或）条件，认为这不会给 Debian 等分发方造成负担。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License
timeline.snippet: Bruce Perens wrote: > Regarding the sending back of modifications, please read the APSL, IBM Public > Source license, or the ATT license and use their text. The APSL is at > http:
timeline.point: Explains the intent behind the modification return clause and asks for specific wording suggestions to improve it.
timeline.point_zh: 解释修改回报条款背后的意图，并请求提供具体的措辞建议以改进该条款。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License
timeline.snippet: From: Alex Nicolaou <anicolao at cgl.uwaterloo.ca> > You may not distribute versions of the software with your patch applied, > although you may include your patches in a subdirec
timeline.point: Criticizes the requirement to return modifications on every edit as impractical and suggests adopting a URL-based method.
timeline.point_zh: 批评每次编辑都须回报修改的要求不切实际，建议采用基于 URL 的方式。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License
timeline.snippet: From: bruce at perens.com (Bruce Perens) > I think you should require that they be marked clearly as modificatied > versions, but you need to allow them to be distributed. Change
timeline.point: Corrects a typo in a previous message, changing "modificatied versions" to "modifications."
timeline.point_zh: 更正前一条消息中的拼写错误，将“modificatied versions”改为“modifications”。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License
timeline.snippet: From: Alex Nicolaou <anicolao at cgl.uwaterloo.ca> > While I agree that this needs to be added to my license, I'm not sure > why modified binary versions really need to be distrib
timeline.point: Recommends using the text from the APSL, IBM, or ATT licenses for the modification return clause.
timeline.point_zh: 建议修改回报条款采用 APSL、IBM 或 ATT 许可证中的文本。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License v1.01
timeline.snippet: I am still soliciting feedback on this license. I've attempted to modify it to address Bruce Perens' comments regarding return of modifications and binary distributions. I believe
timeline.point: Solicits feedback on SOS v1.01, revised to address Bruce Perens' comments on returning modifications and binary distribution, and asserts it now fully conforms to the OSD.
timeline.point_zh: 征求对 SOS v1.01 的反馈，称已按 Bruce Perens 关于修改回馈与二进制分发的意见修改，并认为其现已完全符合 OSD。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License v1.02
timeline.snippet: I am still soliciting feedback on this license. At least send me private mail saying "I like it", or "I hate it". Some reasoning would be nice too. This version has updated clause
timeline.point: Solicits feedback on SOS v1.02, explaining that clause 7 now voids the license if a court order prevents compliance, and asks for reactions even by private mail.
timeline.point_zh: 征求对 SOS v1.02 的反馈，说明第 7 条已改为：若因法院命令等原因无法遵守条款，则许可证作废。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License v1.02
timeline.snippet: Ken Arromdee wrote: > > On Fri, 22 Oct 1999, Alex Nicolaou wrote: > > 3. You may modify your copies of the software, provided that you either > > > > a) publicly distribute your c
timeline.point: Struggles to distinguish between development and distribution for network testing and asks for wording to fix the issue.
timeline.point_zh: 难以在网络测试场景下区分开发与分发，请求提供措辞来解决此问题。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License v1.02
timeline.snippet: On Fri, 22 Oct 1999, Alex Nicolaou wrote: > 3. You may modify your copies of the software, provided that you either > > a) publicly distribute your changes as a source code patch
timeline.point: Argues the license is impractical because it obligates users to distribute patches on every compile cycle.
timeline.point_zh: 认为该许可证不切实际，因为它要求用户在每次编译时都分发补丁。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License v1.02

timeline.point: Suggests adding a time-delayed check-in requirement (e.g., 60 days) to allow for normal development cycles.
timeline.point_zh: 建议增加延迟回报要求（例如 60 天），以顾及正常的开发周期。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License v1.03
timeline.snippet: In this version I have believe the licence addresses all complaints against it so far. More feedback, please! thanks, alex -- SOS - Simple Open Source License version 1.03 Copyrig
timeline.point: Posts SOS v1.03, stating the license now addresses all complaints received so far, and asks for more feedback.
timeline.point_zh: 发布 SOS v1.03，称其已回应迄今所有批评意见，并请求更多反馈。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License v1.03

timeline.point: Notes the patent clause should be restricted to compression ("encoding") only.
timeline.point_zh: 指出专利条款应仅限于压缩（“encoding”）。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License v1.03
timeline.snippet: On Thu, 28 Oct 1999, Alex Nicolaou wrote: > 1. You may distribute complete and verbatim copies of this software and > all supporting files, provided that you do so without any cha
timeline.point: Raises concerns about notice requirements, modification return loopholes, and clauses that restrict execution.

timeline.point: Defends the "all or nothing" license structure to avoid legal ambiguity regarding which parts users can ignore.
timeline.point_zh: 为“all or nothing”（全有或全无）的许可证结构辩护，以避免用户可忽略哪些部分的法律歧义。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License v1.03
timeline.snippet: Hi, please see below. >> > 6. You are not required to distribute your patches under the terms of >> > this license. However, by submitting your patches to the copyright >> > holde
timeline.point: Explains that under European law, a license is void if any clause conflicts with the law.
timeline.point_zh: 解释说根据欧洲法律，如果许可的任何条款与法律冲突，则该许可无效。

timeline.subject: YAOSL - Yet Another Open Source License v1.03
timeline.snippet: Alex Nicolaou wrote: [...] > > This is similar to the above. What if a nation (France for example) ruled that > > something was unenforcable (the 90 days for another example). Thi

timeline.point: Recommends OSI officials contact System76 to discuss OSD and policy problems, encouraging them to use a standard license instead.
timeline.point_zh: 建议OSI官员联系System76讨论OSD和政策问题，并鼓励其改用标准许可证。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] System 76's BeanBooks Public License v1.0
timeline.snippet: On 9/18/2013 4:08 PM, Ken Arromdee wrote: > On Wed, 18 Sep 2013, John Cowan wrote: >>> Sec. 4.3 strikes me as actually conceptually somewhat interesting, >>> inasmuch as many comm
timeline.point: Argues section 4.3 violates OSD 5 or 6 by contractually requiring commercial distributors to obtain a trademark license for lawful uses, treating commercial enterprises differently from non-commercial ones.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 4.3 条要求商业分发者为合法使用取得商标许可，区别对待商业与非商业主体，违反 OSD 5 或 6。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] System 76's BeanBooks Public License v1.0
timeline.snippet: Ken Arromdee scripsit: > > 4.3 - Commercial distribution of the Software requires a > > trademark license agreement and you may be required to > > pay. Using the Software within a
timeline.point: Maintains that the trademark license requirement effectively creates a proprietary software license by charging for commercial redistribution rights.
timeline.point_zh: 坚持认为商标许可要求实际上通过收取商业再分发权利费用而形成专有软件许可。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] System 76's BeanBooks Public License v1.0
timeline.snippet: I have not had time to do this myself but it is probably a reasonable idea. Luis On Sep 19, 2013 7:40 PM, "Bradley M. Kuhn" <bkuhn at ebb.org> wrote: > It seems that at least a fe
timeline.point: Agrees that contacting System76 to discuss the license is a reasonable idea.
timeline.point_zh: 同意联系System76讨论该许可是一个合理的主意。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Contribution Public License
timeline.snippet: Hello, due to me being unable to find a reciprocal software license I'm truly happy with I've been working on developing my own: https://github.com/MoritzMaxeiner/contribution-pub
timeline.point: Presents a draft Contribution Public License — MIT-like in spirit but requiring modifications to be contributed back under the same license — seeking feedback ahead of eventual OSI approval, and explains why RPL-1.5, EFL-2 and MS-RL don't fill this niche.
timeline.point_zh: 发布 Contribution Public License 草案——精神接近 MIT 但要求修改以同一许可证回馈——征求意见，并说明 RPL-1.5、EFL-2、MS-RL 为何不合需求。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Contribution Public License
timeline.snippet: I would not use the word 'Contribute' in clause 2, but instead use the word 'Publish'. 'Contribute' implies more than just publication, at least in common usage in the open source
timeline.point: Suggests replacing 'Contribute' with 'Publish' to avoid confusion, and removing 'to the public' as it is redundant and problematic.
timeline.point_zh: 建议将'Contribute'替换为'Publish'以避免混淆，并删去'to the public'因其冗余且有问题。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Contribution Public License
timeline.snippet: Thanks for the suggestions. If I were to adopt them I think I can go a bit further and shorten clause 2 to this (or do you see any issue with removing the "as follows" part?): 2.
timeline.point: Accepts the suggestion to use 'Publish' and proposes a shortened version of the clause for review.
timeline.point_zh: 接受使用'Publish'的建议，并提出该条款的精简版本供审查。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Contribution Public License

timeline.point: Raises two concerns: the license compels publication of modifications with no time frame while omitting an explicit source-provision requirement, and it lacks a patent grant; proposes GPL-like source obligations and an Apache 2-style patent grant.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License

timeline.point: Argues that grants and obligations are inconsistent and suggests making grants conditional for better legal enforceability.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: I will register my standard objection, which is that 2.2 seems to attempt to restrict private modification. Many countries are starting to recognise the harm of claiming restricti
timeline.point: Objects to clause 2.2 restricting private modification, arguing it attempts to circumvent copyright law exceptions.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Disregarding the specifics of any particular license: In my opinion the spirit (if not the wording) of the "libre" in FLOSS is primarily (and if not should be) about minimizing th
timeline.point: Argues that allowing private modifications places restrictions on source code, contradicting the spirit of "libre."
timeline.point_zh: 认为允许私人修改会对源代码施加限制，与 "libre" 的精神相悖。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Thu, Aug 8, 2019 at 9:44 PM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > In my opinion the spirit (if not the wording) of the "libre" in FLOSS is > primarily (and if not should be)
timeline.point: Argues the proposal creates a new restriction by disallowing privacy for source code that never previously existed publicly, that such privacy restrictions reduce the amount of source code written, and that the community should protect privacy rather than treat forbidding it as protecting liberty.
timeline.point_zh: 认为该提案对从未公开存在的源码施加禁止隐私的新限制,此类限制会减少被编写的源码数量;社区应保护隐私,而非把禁止隐私当作保护自由。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Friday, 9 August 2019 05:36:26 CEST Russell McOrmond wrote: > On Thu, Aug 8, 2019 at 9:44 PM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > > In my opinion the spirit (if not the word
timeline.point: Defends the draft: his primary concern is ensuring derivative source code gets published where the original author wishes it, not how much software gets written; rejects equating derived source code with personal information, citing Kerckhoffs's principle.
timeline.point_zh: 为草案辩护:他的核心关切是确保在原作者希望公开时衍生源码得以发布,而非软件编写量;援引 Kerckhoffs 原则,拒绝将衍生源码与个人信息划等号。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Fri, Aug 9, 2019 at 8:45 AM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > On Friday, 9 August 2019 05:36:26 CEST Russell McOrmond wrote: > > Curious: Since I have the capability to w
timeline.point: Argues that forcing disclosure of code not distributed beyond the author's own computers violates user privacy and inverts FLOSS's purpose of reducing author control; calls the draft's goal proprietary and likens its reasoning to Microsoft's Shared Source program.
timeline.point_zh: 认为强制公开未越出作者自有计算机的代码侵犯用户隐私,颠倒了 FLOSS 削弱作者控制权的初衷;称该草案的目标属专有软件,并将其论证类比微软 Shared Source 计划。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Tue, Aug 13, 2019 at 7:34 PM Russell McOrmond <russellmcormond at gmail.com> wrote: > Is it the act of me typing the software into my computer that offends you? > Obviously, th
timeline.point: States that creating derivative works is restricted by copyright even in private, and authors choose to permit it.
timeline.point_zh: 指出即使在私下创作衍生作品也受著作权限制，而作者选择允许这种行为。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 14, 2019 at 1:30 AM Bruce Perens via License-discuss < license-discuss at lists.opensource.org> wrote: > On Tue, Aug 13, 2019 at 7:34 PM Russell McOrmond < > russellmc
timeline.point: Asks whether OSD-compliant licenses should embrace harmful legal restrictions on private activities simply because they exist.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License

timeline.point: Argues that OSD #3 implies a license forbidding private modifications is not an open source license.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 OSD #3 意味着禁止私人修改的许可证并非开源许可证。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 14, 2019 at 1:45 PM John Cowan <cowan at ccil.org> wrote: > I think that OSD #3 does exactly that. "The license must allow > modifications and derived works [...]" A l
timeline.point: Clarifies that the discussion concerns when distribution terms activate for derivative works, not forbidding the act itself.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Thanks for the clarification. I simply reacted to your saying that private modifications are not necessarily protected by OSD-compliant licenses. On Wed, Aug 14, 2019 at 4:53 PM B
timeline.point: Thanks the sender for the clarification on private modifications and OSD compliance.
timeline.point_zh: 感谢发件人就私人修改及 OSD 合规问题所作的澄清。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wednesday, 14 August 2019 04:33:25 CEST Russell McOrmond wrote: > On Fri, Aug 9, 2019 at 8:45 AM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > > On Friday, 9 August 2019 05:36:26 CES
timeline.point: Objects to the creation of secret derivative work of open source software, arguing nothing in the OSD conflicts with requiring source disclosure upon creation of derivative works; concerned with OSD compliance rather than FLOSS compliance.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 12:38 PM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > Why does my wish for derivative works of certain software to be available > to > the public (and legitimat
timeline.point: Argues copyright should not regulate private activities, so privately made modifications are not 'derivative works'; finds it offensive that OSI would approve licenses encouraging the expansion of copyright into private activities.
timeline.point_zh: 主张版权不应规制私人活动，私下修改不属于“衍生作品”；认为 OSI 批准鼓励版权扩张至私人活动的许可证令人反感。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:00 AM Russell McOrmond <russellmcormond at gmail.com> wrote: > > I am offended by any alleged legitimacy granted to the exclusive rights of > software a
timeline.point: Advises maintaining a collegial tone and questions the limits of protecting private acts that infringe copyright.
timeline.point_zh: 建议保持友善的同行语气，并质疑保护侵犯著作权的私人行为的限度。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell McOrmond wrote: > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 12:38 PM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > > Why does my wish for derivative works of certain software to be available to
timeline.point: Expresses offense at users benefiting from free code while keeping improvements private.
timeline.point_zh: 对用户受益于自由代码却将改进保持私密表示不满。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:16 AM Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org> wrote: > I am offended by the notion that someone may benefit from code that I > released for free, but > would d
timeline.point: Questions how sharing something under specific terms grants others the fundamental right to do as they wish in private.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑依特定条款分享某物如何能赋予他人在私下随心所欲的基本权利。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 2:23 PM Bruce Perens <bruce at perens.com> wrote: > > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:16 AM Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org> wrote: > >> I am offended by the
timeline.point: Argues copyright is a bargain between society and creators, and that copyright holders have no legitimate right to regulate private activities, citing UN UDHR article 27 and Canadian Bill C-11 exceptions (sections 29.22 and 30.6).
timeline.point_zh: 主张版权是社会与创作者之间的契约，版权人没有规制私人活动的正当权利，并援引《世界人权宣言》第27条及加拿大 C-11 法案例外条款。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: > You are trying to state copyright law in reverse, presuming the right to control culture and science is natural and any limitations on that (such as the protection of privacy ri
timeline.point: Notes the moral conflict between personal liberty and creator control, believing private-use restrictions are not in society's best interest.
timeline.point_zh: 指出个人自由与创作者控制之间存在道德冲突，认为私人使用限制不符合社会最佳利益。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell McOrmond wrote: > > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 2:23 PM Bruce Perens <bruce at perens.com <mailto:bruce at perens.com>> wrote: > > > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:16 AM Howar
timeline.point: Cites UDHR article 27(2) to argue authors own their works and dictate license terms; holds that benefiting from free software obliges contributing back, and claims GPL and other OSS licenses' failure to require this drives maintainer burnout.
timeline.point_zh: 援引《世界人权宣言》第27条第2款，主张作者拥有作品并可依许可证决定使用条件；认为从自由软件受益就应回馈，GPL 等 OSS 许可证缺乏此要求导致维护者倦怠。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Hi all, On Wed, Aug 21, 2019, at 12:22, Howard Chu wrote: > Article 27: > (1) Everyone has the right freely to participate in the cultural life > of the community, to enjoy the ar
timeline.point: Warns that forced disclosure of private modifications could endanger users in humanitarian contexts and is contrary to the OSD.
timeline.point_zh: 警告强制披露私人修改可能危及人道主义环境中的用户，且违反 OSD。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019, 15:22 Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org> wrote: > Russell McOrmond wrote: > When you benefit from Free software, you have an obligation to contribute > back, e
timeline.point: States that obligations to provide cash or labor are fundamentally incompatible with open source licenses and would have killed GPLv3 adoption.
timeline.point_zh: 声称提供现金或劳动的义务与开源许可证根本不相容，本会扼杀 GPLv3 的采用。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 2:38 PM Bruce Perens via License-discuss < license-discuss at lists.opensource.org> wrote: > > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:00 AM Russell McOrmond < > russ
timeline.point: Argues extending copyright to private activities is 'a bridge too far' that should disqualify a license from OSI approval, outlines Canadian law's carve-outs of private activities, and worries the FSF and OSI are becoming proprietary minded.
timeline.point_zh: 主张将版权扩展至私人活动是“过分之举”，应使许可证丧失 OSI 批准资格；讨论加拿大法律对私人活动的豁免，并担心 FSF 和 OSI 正变得愈发专有化。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 3:39 PM Christopher Sean Morrison via License-discuss <license-discuss at lists.opensource.org> wrote: > > You are trying to state copyright law in reverse
timeline.point: Argues software licensing is a matter of copyright, patent and contract law offering only a limited bundle of rights, and that using license terms to regulate cloud providers or protect employees falls outside the proper jurisdiction of license agreements.
timeline.point_zh: 认为软件许可属于著作权、专利和合同法范畴，仅授予有限权利；利用许可条款监管云服务商或保护雇员超出了许可协议的适用范围。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 2:16 PM Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org> wrote: > Fwiw, most of the free software I released in the 1980s, before GPL > existed, had the clause > "You are
timeline.point: Argues that forced contributions — requiring private modifications to be made public — are contrary to the FSF's four freedoms and the OSI's OSD, though this is not yet a settled discussion; freedom 0 places no obligations on pure software use.
timeline.point_zh: 认为强制贡献——要求私有修改也须公开——违背 FSF 四大自由与 OSD,但此事尚无定论;freedom 0 不对纯软件使用施加义务。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell McOrmond wrote: > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 2:16 PM Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org <mailto:hyc at openldap.org>> wrote: > > Fwiw, most of the free software I released in
timeline.point: Asserts that requesting improvements benefits the greater good and prevents zero-day vulnerabilities, arguing the FSF erred by not enforcing contribution obligations.
timeline.point_zh: 声称要求改进有利于更大的公益并防止零日漏洞，认为 FSF 未强制回馈义务是错误的。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wednesday, 21 August 2019 22:07:28 CEST Michael Downey wrote: > Hi all, > > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019, at 12:22, Howard Chu wrote: > > Article 27: > > (1) Everyone has the right fre
timeline.point: Suggests restricting private modifications is acceptable for software like compilers, while distinguishing between software use and private derivative work creation.
timeline.point_zh: 建议对编译器等软件限制私人修改尚可接受，并区分软件使用与私人创作衍生作品。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell, please clarify something for me about your opinion about copyright policy: Is any license whatsoever required in order for a private party to copy or modify a work of sof
timeline.point: Asks Russell to clarify whether any license is required for a private party to copy or modify software for private purposes, asserting software is copyrightable under US law and Berne, and questioning how anyone could avoid a license for private uses.
timeline.point_zh: 请 Russell 澄清：私人复制、修改软件是否需要任何许可证；指出软件在美国法律及《伯尔尼公约》下受版权保护，并质疑私人使用如何能避开许可证。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wednesday, 21 August 2019 19:59:03 CEST Russell McOrmond wrote: > On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 12:38 PM Moritz Maxeiner <mm at ucw.sh> wrote: > > Why does my wish for derivative wor
timeline.point: Defends the legitimacy of copyright holder concerns and criticizes the previous implication as hostile, bowing out of the sub-thread.
timeline.point_zh: 为版权持有者关切的正当性辩护，批评前述暗示具有敌意，并退出该子讨论。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Howard Chu dixit: >A standard license clause of this form would also have ended the >debate over disclosure of zero-day vulnerabilities and other such >nonsense that plagues today
timeline.point: Howard Chu dixit: >A standard license clause of this form would also have ended the >debate over disclosure of zero-day vulnerabilities and other such >nonsense that plagues today

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: > > You are trying to state copyright law in reverse, presuming the right to control culture and science is natural and any limitations on that (such as the protection of privacy
timeline.point: Pushes back that the lengthy philosophical reply reads more as soapboxing than discourse, and reasserts that imposing terms based on creator rights is not obviously illegitimate — attempts to use licensing to keep code open are entirely consistent with the OSD.
timeline.point_zh: 批评对方冗长的哲学式回复更像说教而非讨论，并重申基于创作者权利施加条款的立场并非明显不合法，用许可保持代码开放与 OSD 完全一致。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 8:39 PM Lawrence Rosen <lrosen at rosenlaw.com> wrote: > Russell, please clarify something for me about your opinion about > copyright policy: Is any licen
timeline.point: Argues whether private modification requires permission depends on jurisdiction, purpose, and source; as a matter of policy the FSF and OSI should reject licenses that regulate private modification, and lists ways to avoid such licenses.
timeline.point_zh: 认为私人修改是否需要许可取决于辖区、用途和来源；从政策角度 FSF 和 OSI 应拒绝规范私人修改的许可证，并列举规避此类许可证的方法。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell, what you said is not true in the United States. I dare not speak to Canadian law. Russell wrote: * What is the purpose of the copying or modification of the work. If the
timeline.point: Corrects Russell on US law: compatibility copying requires the copyright holder's permission (unlike Canada's exceptions), and backups only for holders of licensed copies per 17 USC 117; rejects amending the law or forking OSI/FSF, saying don't change our law or licenses without permission.
timeline.point_zh: 纠正Russell关于美国法的说法：兼容性复制需版权人许可，备份仅限获许可副本持有者（17 USC 117）；反对修改法律或分叉OSI/FSF，称未经许可勿改法律或许可证。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Thorsten Glaser wrote: > Howard Chu dixit: > >> A standard license clause of this form would also have ended the >> debate over disclosure of zero-day vulnerabilities and other su
timeline.point: Disagrees with the desert island test, arguing that sending modifications back doesn't immediately publish them and best-effort reporting is reasonable.
timeline.point_zh: 不认同荒岛测试，认为发回修改并非立即公开发布，尽力报告是合理的。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Thursday 22 August 2019 06:17, Howard Chu wrote: > The requirement to send modifications back doesn't prevent anyone from using the code. You > could call it best-effort, or at
timeline.point: Clarifies that in Free Software, the requirement to send modifications back applies only upon distribution, not for in-house changes.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清在自由软件中，发回修改的要求仅适用于分发时，不适用于内部改动。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Thu, Aug 22, 2019, 00:18 Howard Chu <hyc at openldap.org> wrote: > I don't believe this test is conclusive. Sending modifications back to the > code's original author doesn't i
timeline.point: Argues that privileging the original author creates badgeware, requiring publication of private changesets is ineffective, and the license seeks proprietary control.
timeline.point_zh: 认为优待原作者会催生 badgeware，要求公开私人变更集收效甚微，且该许可证意在谋求专有控制。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Johnny A. Solbu dixit: >On Thursday 22 August 2019 06:17, Howard Chu wrote: >> Two of these which often appear necessary are the Chinese Dissident >> test (requirement to publish
timeline.point: Insists that the desert island test is valid and that Free Software never requires sending modifications back, only passing them along to recipients.
timeline.point_zh: 坚持荒岛测试有效，且自由软件从不要求将修改发回，只要求传递给接收者。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Thursday 22 August 2019 20:55, Thorsten Glaser wrote: > Some Free Software has a requirement to pass the modifications along to the > recipient if you distribute the work, but
timeline.point: Clarifies that the previous comment was referencing Linus Torvalds' view that publishing changes on a project site counts as sending code back.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清前述评论援引的是 Linus Torvalds 的观点，即在项目网站上发布更改即算作发回代码。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Johnny A. Solbu dixit: >He have said in inverviews that he wants code back. He wants the >changes people use, but says that publishing the changed code on the >projects own site i
timeline.point: Notes that while projects often want code back, the actual license only requires distributing source to recipients, not sending it to upstream.
timeline.point_zh: 指出虽然项目常希望收回代码，但许可证实际只要求向接收者分发源码，而非发给上游。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On 8/21/2019 7:33 PM, Lawrence Rosen wrote: > > Russell, please clarify something for me about your opinion about > copyright policy: Is any license whatsoever required in order f
timeline.point: Expresses confusion about fair use in software and questions whether OSI should support licenses that weaken it.
timeline.point_zh: 对软件中的合理使用表示困惑，并质疑 OSI 是否应支持削弱合理使用的许可证。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:35 PM Lawrence Rosen <lrosen at rosenlaw.com> wrote: > I appreciate your discussion of preferred policies, but that has nothing > to do with license-dis
timeline.point: Argues the OSD's purpose is drawing the line between software proprietors' and users' interests, and that FSF/OSI approval of licenses demanding disclosure of private modifications or triggered by interface use is a radical departure that could have blocked tools like LibreOffice and Samba.
timeline.point_zh: 认为 OSD 的宗旨正是划清软件所有者与用户利益的界限；FSF/OSI 批准要求披露私有修改或因接口使用而触发的许可证是激进转变，可能令 LibreOffice、Samba 等工具无法诞生。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Roger Fujii wrote: > Now I'm confused. Are you saying there is no "fair use" when the target is software? While one can weaken" fair use" via the license, is this a good idea for
timeline.point: Clarifies that fair use is a defense to infringement but a poor basis for claiming rights to commercial software distribution.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清合理使用是针对侵权的抗辩理由，但作为主张商业软件发行权利的依据并不充分。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: Russell McOrmond wrote: > Guesses about license interpretation by courts, and unintended consequences from that interpretation of licenses, is entirely on-topic for this forum. Th
timeline.point: Cautiones that guesses about license interpretation will not convince a court, since courts interpret existing law as it stands — citing the industry's attempt to win a copyright exception for APIs.
timeline.point_zh: 提醒对许可证解释的猜测无法说服法院，法院只会按现有法律解释——并以业界寻求 API 版权例外为例。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] For Public Comment: The Libre Source License
timeline.snippet: On 8/23/2019 1:23 PM, Lawrence Rosen wrote: > > Roger Fujii wrote: > > Now I'm confused. Are you saying there is no "fair use" when the > target is software? While one can weaken"
timeline.point: Argues that if fair use is a right, some modifications should be covered, and suggests licenses and OSI should clarify their stance on fair use.
timeline.point_zh: 主张若合理使用是一项权利，某些修改应被涵盖，并建议许可证和OSI澄清对合理使用的立场。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: I am reaching out to community to collect feedback on the proposed license. Here is text of License: https://github.com/trplfoundation/trpl-license/blob/main/LICENSE Thanks, Jay
timeline.point: Submits the TRPL Foundation license for community feedback.
timeline.point_zh: 提交TRPL Foundation许可证以征求社区反馈。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: Jay, If you intend to ask for critique, there’s quite a bit — from nitpicking details to fundamental flaws. I’ll list some of the apparent ones below as I read the license text. I
timeline.point: TRPL 1.0's preamble reads like a manifesto, its definitions are overbroad, and the Combined Work provision could force release of proprietary source — the license has little practical use since adopting it endangers the rest of one's software.
timeline.point_zh: TRPL 1.0 序言似宣言，定义过宽，Combined Work 条款或迫使公开专有软件源码；使用它将威胁其余软件，几乎无实用价值。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: The functional output restrictionn would keep it from being an Open Source license. It's pretty clearly a use restriction. Bruce Perens K6BP On Wed, Dec 3, 2025, 08:23 Gil Yehuda
timeline.point: States the functional output restriction disqualifies the license as Open Source because it is a use restriction.
timeline.point_zh: 指出功能性输出限制属于使用限制，使该许可证不符合开源条件。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: Thank You Gil for feedback.You identified a critical logical loop (the 'Postman problem') that would have made compliance impossible. Maybe adding this address your poins: 1. Addi
timeline.point: Acknowledges feedback on logical loops and proposes adding exceptions for system tools to ensure the license is 'Stronger than AGPL' but runnable.
timeline.point_zh: 接受关于逻辑循环的反馈，提议为系统工具添加例外，以确保许可证“Stronger than AGPL”但仍可运行。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: Great, let’s talk about that goal: “Stronger than AGPL” I believe AGPL failed to meet its original intent. I understand the motivation on the part of the FSF folks to close the “l
timeline.point: Questions the "Stronger than AGPL" goal, arguing AGPL failed its original intent and is often used to leverage commercial licensing deals rather than promote software freedom. Says the new license offers nothing not already available, and will fail like AGPL unless it fixes why AGPL fell short.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑"比 AGPL 更强"的目标：AGPL 未能实现初衷，常被用作商业授权筹码而非促进软件自由；新许可证未提供已有之外的价值，若不解决 AGPL 失败的原因将同样失败。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: How so? It's easy to say that any limitation is a use restriction - saying that one has to include a copy of the license discriminates against those who don't want to. So can you
timeline.point: Challenges the assertion that the output restriction is a use restriction, asking how it discriminates against a field of endeavor.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑输出限制属于使用限制的说法，询问其如何歧视某一应用领域。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: OK, I dismissed the license quickly, which might leave the submitter in the dark. Thus: The term in question is the following: *4.1 Functional OutputIf the Program is used to gene
timeline.point: The Functional Output clause is unenforceable as a copyright condition: compiler output is functional and uncopyrightable under 17 USC 102(b), and it bars code under any other license. The license lacks legal solidity, so its community shouldn't be called Open Source.
timeline.point_zh: Functional Output 条款无法执行：编译产物具功能性，按 17 USC 102(b) 不受版权保护，且排斥其他许可证；法律上不成立，不宜称 Open Source。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: This was garble: "no significant copyrightable component of the original work persists in the created executable." It should be: "no significant copyrightable component of the com
timeline.point: Corrects a typo in the previous message regarding the persistence of copyrightable components.
timeline.point_zh: 更正上一条消息中关于可版权组件持续存在的笔误。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: Gil wrote: when licenses say “This includes, but is not limited to” that automatically creates a speed bump where a reader (and their lawyer) have to imagine if this includes some
timeline.point: Questions the claim that 'includes but is not limited to' creates broad legal scope, asking for case law examples.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑“includes but is not limited to”会产生宽泛法律范围的说法,要求提供判例示例。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: On 12/3/2025 11:40 AM, Bruce Perens via License-discuss wrote: > OK, I dismissed the license quickly, which might leave the submitter > in the dark. Thus: > > The term in question
timeline.point: Compiler output is copyrightable and possibly derivative, making the requirement acceptable quasi-copyleft; an OSD9 issue arises only if output isn't truly derivative, and Jay's comments read as reasons the license isn't ready for submission.
timeline.point_zh: 编译器输出可获版权且可能构成衍生作品，故该要求是可接受的准copyleft；仅当输出非真正衍生才有OSD9问题，Jay的意见像是在说明该许可证尚不宜提交。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: Sorry, I meant to say I agree with Gil's comment's on the license, not Jay (the license submitter). Pam Pamela S. Chestek Chestek Legal 4641 Post St. Unit 4316 El Dorado Hills, CA
timeline.point: Clarifies that the previous comment agreed with Gil's critique of the license, not with the submitter.
timeline.point_zh: 澄清前一条评论是赞同Gil对该许可证的批评,而非赞同提交者。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: On 12/3/2025 1:56 PM, Pamela Chestek wrote: > > But that seems orthogonal to your point. Your hypo seems to be that > the compiler is under this license ("infringes the copyright
timeline.point: Cites the GCC runtime exception as a precedent for allowing compilation of non-GPL programs with covered libraries.
timeline.point_zh: 引用GCC runtime exception作为先例,允许将非GPL程序与所涉库一起编译。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: On Wed, Dec 3, 2025 at 1:58 PM Pamela Chestek <pamela.chestek at opensource.org> wrote: > > On 12/3/2025 11:40 AM, Bruce Perens via License-discuss wrote: > > It is not an accurat
timeline.point: Compiler-generated code is purely functional—a translation bearing the same copyright as its input—so the Functional Output terms are unenforceable; "compatible" is left undefined, and this is a work-processed-by-another-work issue, not a derivative-work issue.
timeline.point_zh: 编译器生成的代码纯属功能性翻译，版权同于输入，故Functional Output条款不可执行；compatible未定义；属作品被另一作品处理的问题，非衍生作品问题。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: On 12/3/25 10:12 AM, Gil Yehuda wrote: > I believe AGPL failed to meet its original intent. I understand the > motivation on the part of the FSF folks to close the “loophole" that
timeline.point: Views the AGPL as successful but warns that pushing beyond its legal limits for a 'more free' license risks enforceability issues.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: > any "more free" license is going to be at least walking the border of what's possible in a license. But not necessarily a more formal contract. On Wed, Dec 3, 2025 at 4:19 PM Jo

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] Total Reciprocity Public License (TRPL v1.0)
timeline.snippet: It just struck me as odd, because I _always_ use just those words: "including, but not limited to", out of fear that some court somewhere will think otherwise. I agree that the pr
timeline.point: Agrees that the discussion is academic, noting that similar licensing misconceptions appear frequently.

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] US Army Research Laboratory Open Source License proposal
timeline.sender: Karan, Cem F CIV USARMY RDECOM ARL
timeline.snippet: Hi, my name is Cem Karan. I work for the US Army Research Laboratory (ARL) in Adelphi, MD. I'm in charge of defining the Open Source policy for ARL. As a part of this, we need a l
timeline.point: Submits the U.S. Army Research Laboratory Open Source License (ARL OSL) 0.2, a modified Apache 2.0 that removes copyright references to cover US Government public-domain works, and asks for comments.
timeline.point_zh: 提交 ARL OSL 0.2——修改自 Apache 2.0、移除版权字样以覆盖美国政府公有领域作品的许可证——并征求意见。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] US Army Research Laboratory Open Source License proposal
timeline.snippet: On Fri, Jul 22, 2016 at 11:01 PM, Karan, Cem F CIV USARMY RDECOM ARL (US) <cem.f.karan.civ at mail.mil> wrote: > Hi, my name is Cem Karan. I work for the US Army Research Laborato
timeline.point: Suggests using dual licensing with a public domain dedication and Apache-2.0 to avoid creating a new license.
timeline.point_zh: 建议采用公有领域贡献加Apache-2.0的双许可方式，以避免创建新许可证。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] US Army Research Laboratory Open Source License proposal
timeline.snippet: Cem Karan wrote: > Most of our researchers work for the US Federal Government and under US copyright law any works they produce during the course of their duties do not have copyr
timeline.point: Argues US government works are public domain domestically and a standard license like Apache 2.0 suffices for foreign use.
timeline.point_zh: 认为美国政府作品在国内属公有领域，在国外使用Apache 2.0等标准许可证即可。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] US Army Research Laboratory Open Source License proposal
timeline.snippet: Karan, Cem F CIV USARMY RDECOM ARL (US) scripsit: > Finally, there is opinion within the US Government that while there is no US > copyright protection, copyright attaches outside
timeline.point: Suggests the US government holds foreign copyright and recommends retaining 'copyright holder' terminology for contractors.
timeline.point_zh: 认为美国政府持有国外版权，建议对承包商保留'copyright holder'术语。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] US Army Research Laboratory Open Source License proposal
timeline.snippet: Is that the correct interpretation of the Berne convention? The convention assigns copyright to foreigners of a signatory state with at least as strong protection as own nationals
timeline.point: Questions if the US government holds foreign copyright, suggesting no copyright exists worldwide if it does not exist domestically.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑美国政府是否持有国外版权，指出若国内无版权则全球均无版权。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] US Army Research Laboratory Open Source License proposal
timeline.snippet: On 22/07/16 22:01, Karan, Cem F CIV USARMY RDECOM ARL (US) wrote: > Unfortunately, we cannot directly use the Apache 2 license for all of our > code. Most of our researchers work
timeline.point: Questions if OSI approves contracts and asks what needs protecting if the work is already in the public domain.
timeline.point_zh: 质疑OSI是否批准合同，并询问若作品已属公有领域还有什么需要保护。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] US Army Research Laboratory Open Source License proposal
timeline.snippet: On Fri, Jul 22, 2016 at 11:23 PM, Lawrence Rosen <lrosen at rosenlaw.com> wrote: > > It is true that this public domain result doesn't apply outside the U.S. But > if you apply a
timeline.point: Asks if the lack of US government copyright applies globally or if a separate license is needed outside the USA.
timeline.point_zh: 询问美国政府无版权是否全球适用，还是美国以外需要单独的许可证。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] US Army Research Laboratory Open Source License proposal
timeline.snippet: Hi, Yes I am suggesting that if the country of origin of the work does not assign copyright to the work then no copyright is assigned world-wide. My reasoning is that there is no
timeline.point: Argues that works not copyrighted in their country of origin have no copyright anywhere, so the license is void for lack of an underlying right, and advises the US Army to adopt CC0 like the Dutch government.
timeline.point_zh: 认为作品在起源国不受版权保护则在全世界也无版权，许可因缺乏所授权利而失效，并建议美国陆军像荷兰政府一样采用 CC0。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] US Army Research Laboratory Open Source License proposal
timeline.snippet: > I have personally, on occasion, considered filing a Freedom of Information Act request for useful government code to see if that works to pry free software from government hands
timeline.point: Encourages filing a FOIA request and explains the legal ambiguity regarding software as an agency record.
timeline.point_zh: 鼓励提交FOIA请求，并解释软件作为机构记录在法律上的模糊性。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] U.S. Army Research Laboratory Open Source License (ARL OSL) 0.4.0
timeline.sender: Karan, Cem F CIV USARMY RDECOM ARL
timeline.snippet: I've incorporated some suggested changes into the ARL OSL, and bumped the version number to reflect this. The new text is both below and attached, and can be diffed with the text
timeline.point: Posts ARL OSL version 0.4.0 incorporating suggested changes: replacing 'Apache' with 'ARL OSL', adding 'where copyright exists' to clause 2, and adding a new clause 10.
timeline.point_zh: 发布 ARL OSL 0.4.0，纳入建议的修改：将“Apache”改为“ARL OSL”、在第 2 条加入“where copyright exists”、并新增第 10 条。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] U.S. Army Research Laboratory Open Source License (ARL OSL) 0.4.0
timeline.snippet: Has this been reviewed by the ARL Office of Chief Counsel? I know the army has an intellectual property counsel as part of the JAG/USALSA out at Ft. Belvoir. You also have a tech
timeline.point: Advises seeking review from ARL legal counsel and the tech transfer office due to complex regulations.
timeline.point_zh: 建议因法规复杂，寻求ARL法律顾问和技术转让办公室的审查。

timeline.subject: [License-discuss] U.S. Army Research Laboratory Open Source License (ARL OSL) 0.4.0
timeline.snippet: On Thu, Jul 28, 2016 at 3:50 PM, Karan, Cem F CIV USARMY RDECOM ARL (US) <cem.f.karan.civ at mail.mil> wrote: > "License" shall mean the terms and conditions for use, reproduction
timeline.point: Suggests updating the section count and adding 'if copyright exists' conditions, and asks why a severability clause was omitted.
timeline.point_zh: 建议更新条款数量并添加'if copyright exists'条件，并询问为何省略可分割性条款。
